ELESSAR SYSTEMS INC.

Training. Left of Launch.

POSITION DESCRIPTION

Chief Executive Officer

Founding executive of a new defense technology company commercializing Q2 Holodeck™, an immersive training platform for unmanned aircraft systems (UAS) and counter-UAS (C-UAS) decision-making.

POSITION Chief Executive Officer (Co-Founder)

COMPANY Elessar Systems Inc. (Q2 Holodeck™ training platform)

REPORTS TO Board of Directors

DIRECT REPORTS Chief Technology Officer; Chief of Staff; Chief Operating Officer, Director of Business Development; future CRO, CFO/Controller, and Head of Delivery

LOCATION Remote

EMPLOYMENT TYPE Full-time, exempt

Position Summary

The Chief Executive Officer is a co-founder and principal of Elessar Systems Inc., holds full profit-and-loss accountability, and reports to the Board of Directors. The CEO sets the company’s strategy, raises capital, leads government go-to-market, and builds the team to execute on that strategy. In the first eighteen months, the CEO will personally lead customer pursuits, fundraising, and pricing decisions and will be accountable for the company’s first major contract awards.

About Elessar

Elessar is a newly formed defense technology company commercializing Q2 Holodeck™, a browser-based, AI/ML-driven, scenario-based training platform that trains security, force protection, and first-responder personnel to identify a drone, select a lawful and effective response, and report the incident before a real event occurs. The platform runs on The Makusudi Game™, a patented decision-training methodology incubated at Q2IMPACT™, and scores each decision against the authorities and rules of engagement applicable to the customer’s site.

Q2 Holodeck™ is offered as a hosted SaaS, with dedicated and customer-hosted deployments available, subject to technical validation. It serves DoD and DOE/NNSA protective forces, federal and SLTT law enforcement, critical-infrastructure operators, corrections, private entities, and allied nations. As a software product, it enables thousands of personnel to train simultaneously, without the classroom, range, and instructor constraints of traditional schoolhouse training. The market is still early, and the CEO will have the opportunity to set the training standard for AI/ML-driven, dynamic, decision-based training capabilities.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities (approximate % of time)

Ø Strategy and Commercial Model (15%). Set the company’s strategy and market-entry sequence across federal, state and local, and critical-infrastructure markets; finalize pricing and packaging for all deployment modes; protect and extend the company’s intellectual property; and position Q2 Holodeck™ as the reference standard for C-UAS decision training.

Ø Capital Formation and Finance (20%). Lead equity fundraising; pursue non-dilutive funding, including SBIR/STTR, OTA, and program-office awards; own the budget, burn rate, and runway; and establish the finance, accounting, and contract-cost infrastructure required to scale.

Ø Business Development and Capture (30%). Own revenue, pipeline, and forecast; personally lead early-stage pursuits and close reference customers; establish repeatable contracting pathways (CRADA, government purchase card, sole source, and OTA); convert demonstrations into awards; and build relationships with partners and prime contractors.

Ø Product and Delivery Oversight (10%). Set roadmap priorities with the CTO; clearly distinguish fielded and planned capabilities in all external communications; turn custom scenario development into a repeatable process; and build delivery, support, and training-effectiveness measures that drive renewals.

Ø Organization and Talent (10%). Recruit revenue, finance, and delivery leadership ahead of need; build the founding team; and set the company's culture, planning cadence, and accountability standards.

Ø Governance, Compliance, and Risk (10%). Report accurately and promptly to the Board; ensure compliance with ISO 27001, FedRAMP or equivalent authorizations, export controls (ITAR and EAR), and security requirements; manage concentration, accreditation, key-person, and IP risks; and enforce ethical standards in government or commercial sales.

Ø External Representation (5%). Serve as the company’s principal spokesperson to customers, agency and congressional leadership, industry, media, and investors, and contribute to the policy debate on C-UAS authorities and training standards.

Key Performance Objectives

The Board expects the following outcomes over the first twenty-four months. The CEO will set specific targets at the time of hire, and the Board will review them quarterly.

OBJECTIVE HOW SUCCESS IS MEASURED HORIZON

Capital formation Priced round or non-dilutive award closed, funding at least eighteen months of runway against a credible plan Months 1–9

First revenue Signed multi-seat agreements, including at least one named reference customer willing to speak publicly Months 3–12

Contract vehicles At least one executed CRADA, OTA, or sole-source award, with a documented, repeatable path for follow-on work with government and private-sector customers Months 6–15

Compliance and delivery Progress toward ISO 27001, CMMC 2.0, and FedRAMP certification, including a GCC High environment accredited for CUI Months 6–24

Team and pipeline Revenue, finance, and delivery leadership hired; qualified pipeline covering the following year’s plan Months 1–24

Requirements

Qualifications

Required

Ø Education. Bachelor’s degree required.

Ø Experience. Fifteen or more years of progressively senior leadership, including at least five years as a CEO, general manager, division president, or other executive with profit-and-loss responsibility.

Ø Growth record. Demonstrated success scaling a technology, services, products, or software business from early revenue to a durable commercial model, including ownership of pricing and go-to-market strategy.

Ø Market exposure. Direct experience selling to or delivering for U.S. federal, defense, public safety, critical infrastructure, or business-to-business customers.

Ø Capital formation. Experience leading or advising on capital raises (venture, strategic, or non-dilutive) or on mergers and acquisitions.

Ø Financial acumen, including budgeting, cash management, unit economics, and the fiduciary and governance obligations of a company officer.

Ø Work authorization. Eligible to work in the United States.

Ø Travel. Able to travel approximately 25–30% for customer demonstrations, agency engagements, industry events, and investor meetings.

Preferred

Ø Advanced degree in business, engineering, national security, public policy, STEM, or a related field.

Ø Background in counter-UAS, air defense, force protection, homeland security, or critical infrastructure protection.

Ø Experience delivering or implementing SaaS solutions.

Ø Familiarity with the DoD Planning, Programming, Budgeting, and Execution (PPBE) process.

Ø A record of taking a company from pre-revenue to a recurring-revenue sales pipeline.

Benefits

Compensation and Benefits

Ø Base salary of USD 200,000-250,000 per year, based on experience and the company’s capital position at the time of hire.

Ø Performance bonus. A milestone-based bonus of 25% to 50% of base salary is paid upon achievement of the Board-approved objectives above, such as closing the first funding round or securing the first contract award.

Ø Equity. Founder-level equity of 10% to 15%, vesting over four years with a one-year cliff and acceleration upon a qualifying change of control.

Ø Benefits. Medical, dental, and vision coverage; 401(k) with matching; unlimited paid time off; and clearance-related and professional expenses.

Equal Employment Opportunity: Elessar, a subsidiary of Q2IMPACT™, is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate based on race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, national origin, age, disability, marital status, protected veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state, or local law. Reasonable accommodations are available to applicants and employees with disabilities upon request.

Money is moving onto the internet, and the shift has a name: Open Money. This is money that is open, portable, agentic, and owned by you. MetaMask spent the last ten years building it; with 100M+ downloads, users in ~190 countries, and trillions in cumulative transaction volume, it's the most trusted self-custodial financial platform on the internet. Now we're building the operating system for your money: one place to hold, move, grow, and use anything you own. Join a remote-first, global team rebuilding how money works: a problem that touches everyone, every day.

About the role

MetaMask is the world's leading self-custodial wallet — and the primary gateway for hundreds of millions of people into the onchain economy. Our Trading features sit at the heart of that experience: enabling users to place a swap, a perp trade, a prediction market trade, or an investment in Real-World-Assets (RWA) with confidence.

We're looking for a strategic, data-informed, and user-obsessed Senior Product Marketing Manager to own the positioning and growth of these features. This is one of the highest-leverage roles in the MetaMask marketing organisation — sitting at the intersection of product strategy, go-to-market execution, and long-term brand trust.

You'll report to our Product Marketing Director and work across Product, Growth, Brand, Business Development, and Partner Marketing to ensure every launch and lifecycle initiative is anchored in insight, competitive differentiation, and measurable impact.

What you'll do

Strategy

  • Define and execute end-to-end GTM strategy for features within Trading across global markets — from opportunity sizing and positioning through to launch and lifecycle optimisation
  • Partner with Product leads to shape roadmap priorities based on market insight, user behaviour, and growth potential
  • Act as a strategic thought partner to Product and Growth, representing user needs and market realities in decision-making
  • Influence long-term product strategy and monetisation through competitive analysis, segmentation, and market research

GTM and product growth

  • Lead product and feature launches, crafting narratives that resonate with crypto traders and holders,
  • Drive lifecycle marketing initiatives that increase awareness, activation, and retention across Trading funnels
  • Partner with Growth and Analytics to identify friction points and opportunities within user journeys, translating insights into programmes that move key metrics — conversion, volume, retention
  • Ensure strong measurement and continuous iteration — every campaign should have clear success metrics and documented learnings

Cross-functional collaboration

  • Collaborate with Product, Brand, Growth, Communications, Business Development, and Customer Support to deliver integrated campaigns that connect product value to cultural relevance
  • Align cross-functional stakeholders and manage timelines, priorities, and expectations to ensure seamless execution
  • Partner with Data and Product to monitor performance, share learnings, and continually refine GTM approaches

Brand and community

  • Strengthen MetaMask's reputation as a trusted, user-first brand in the Trading community
  • Support education, community, and influencer programmes that drive awareness and confidence — particularly among emerging market segments
  • Ensure consistency in storytelling across all surfaces, from lifecycle emails to content and brand campaigns

What you'll bring

  • 6 to 8+ years in product marketing, ideally within fintech, crypto, or a high-growth consumer tech environment
  • Demonstrated success leading complex product launches and lifecycle growth initiatives with measurable outcomes
  • Strong strategic thinking and storytelling ability — able to turn complex product concepts into clear, compelling narratives
  • Analytical and outcome-driven; comfortable interpreting data and using insight to inform both marketing and product strategy
  • Exceptional cross-functional communication, influence, and project leadership skills
  • Deep curiosity about web3, DeFi, and onchain user behaviour — or direct experience in the crypto ecosystem
  • Nice to have: experience in leading GTM for perps trading and prediction markets products and leading GTM to Asia audience.

Don't meet all the requirements? Don't sweat it. We’re passionate about building a diverse team of humans and as such, if you think you've got what it takes for our chaotic-but-fun, remote-friendly, start-up environment—apply anyway, detailing your relevant transferable skills in your cover letter. While we have a pretty good idea of what we need, we're ready for you to challenge our thinking on who needs to be in this role.

The salary range listed for this role applies to US-based candidates only. Compensation for candidates based outside the US (including Canada, EMEA, and LATAM) will be determined based on location, experience, and skills during the interview process, and may differ from the listed US range.

US pay range (not including bonus, equity or other benefits)
$146,000—$220,000 USD

In the rapidly evolving Web3 space, we believe that everyone is a builder. This expansive paradigm requires a range of backgrounds, talents, skills, and experiences to influence and shape the future. At MetaMask, this diversity fuels our ability to shift control and redefine the realm of possibility. We are committed to ensuring that our technology empowers people and communities through decentralized technologies. We welcome the range of perspectives and differences and celebrate them. We're excited to see how your unique skills as a builder can contribute to our vision, drive innovation, and help us shape a more inclusive Web3.

Senior Generative AI Engineer

Background

We are looking for a Senior Generative AI Engineer to design, build, and ship production-grade Generative AI and Agentic AI applications that delivery business value across the organization. This role is focused on building AI applications and services at scale. You will be responsible for building robust, secure, and highly scalable systems that integrate with leading cloud-based AI services.

You will work alongside product managers, designers, and other engineers as an individual contributor. You are expected to own features end-to-end, and to deliver high-quality, reusable code that scales beyond a single use case.

Key Responsibilities

Software Engineering and Execution

  • Design, build, and ship production-grade Generative and Agentic AI features and applications
  • Own features end-to-end from technical design through implementation, testing, deployment and operation
  • Build reusable, well-abstracted components and shared utilities (e.g., RAG building blocks, agent scaffolding, evaluation harnesses, prompt utilities) to enable faster delivery of future Generative and Agentic AI products
  • Build multi-agent systems using frameworks such as LangChain, LangGraph, Claude Agent SDK and Google ADK
  • Integrate with leading LLM and foundation model APIs, including Azure OpenAI, Google Vertex AI, and AWS Bedrock
  • Build Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) pipelines, including document ingestion, chunking strategies, embeddings, vector search, and re-ranking
  • Build clean, well-tested RESTful and/or gRPC APIs with a focus on reliability, security, and performance
  • Implement observability, tracing, evaluation, guardrails for Generative and Agentic AI applications
  • Deploy and operate services on major cloud providers (e.g., GCP, AWS, and Azure) leveraging managed services
  • Participate actively in code reviews and design discussions, sharing knowledge with peers

Required Qualifications

  • 5-7 years of professional software engineering experience with at least 3 years of experience building AI/ML software products
  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science or a related field (Master's degree preferred)
  • Strong proficiency in Python, with deep software engineering fundamentals (abstraction, modularity, system design, testing, performance)
  • Hands-on experience building and shipping Generative and Agentic AI applications, including LLM integration, prompt engineering, and/or agentic workflows
  • Practical experience integrating cloud-hosted LLM APIs such as Azure OpenAI, Vertex AI, and/or AWS Bedrock
  • Experience with agent frameworks (e.g., LangChain, LangGraph, Google ADK, Claude Agent SDK) and vector databases (e.g., Pinecone, Weaviate, pgvector, Open Search, AlloyDB)
  • Hands-on experience with Google Cloud Platform (GCP), Amazon Web Services (AWS), or Azure
  • Solid understanding of API design, distributed systems, and cloud-native architecture
  • Track record of taking systems from design through production deployment and operation

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience with containerization and orchestration (Docker, Kubernetes)
  • Knowledge of Generative AI Risk Management frameworks (NIST RFM)
  • Experience supporting developer platforms or internal tooling

jobs.description:
Cos'è Blox Space?

Blox Space lavora al centro dell'economia tech,in partnership con un network di oltre 70 realtà attive nel mondo dell'AI, del software, della cybersecurity e delle Freedom Technologies, impegnate nello sviluppo di infrastrutture, prodotti e servizi legati all'economia digitale, alla data protection e al futuro del denaro.
﻿Aiutiamo a connettere i talenti con questo ecosistema, operando come Talent Bridge tra le ambizioni di crescita dei professionisti e le opportunità offerte dal nostro network.
﻿In questo momento stiamo supportando una delle nostre partner companies nella ricerca di un LLM Fine-Tuning Engineer, e se pensi di essere il profilo giusto, ci piacerebbe conoscerti.

Il Ruolo

L'azienda è una startup di cybersecurity italiana che costruisce sistemi di sicurezza autonomi: individuano vulnerabilità sconosciute, prioritizzano il rischio reale e distribuiscono le correzioni senza intervento umano, con un focus sui binari compilati, perché è quello che gira davvero in produzione. È un team early, pre-seed, fondato da ricercatori di sicurezza e accademici di primo piano.
﻿Cerchiamo un LLM Fine-Tuning Engineer che adatti, valuti e metta in produzione modelli linguistici open-weight, ma piegati a un unico scopo: trovare e capire vulnerabilità. Per questo cerchiamo una persona fortemente orientata alla cybersecurity, che non si limiti ad addestrare modelli ma capisca il dominio su cui lavorano. Non è un ruolo di prompt engineering: è l'intero ciclo di post-training, dal design dei dataset al fine tuning, dalla generazione di dati sintetici alla valutazione, fino al deploy in ambienti locali, privati o ristretti.
﻿Non cerchiamo il curriculum perfetto, cerchiamo la testa giusta. Cerchiamo chi sa trasformare un foundation model in un sistema affidabile e specifico per il compito, sa quando il fine tuning è la strada giusta e quando invece conviene prompting, retrieval, orchestrazione o tooling, e porta con sé una vera sensibilità per il mindset di chi attacca.
﻿Le responsabilità di un LLM Fine-Tuning Engineer in questo contesto possono spaziare dal fine tuning e dall'adattamento di LLM open-weight per casi d'uso di sicurezza, interni o rivolti al cliente, al confronto tra approcci di post-training (SFT, tecniche parameter-efficient come LoRA e QLoRA, preference tuning come DPO dove serve, full fine tuning quando giustificato), dalla costruzione e pulizia di dataset di qualità e dalla generazione di dati sintetici alla definizione di metodi di valutazione che vanno oltre i benchmark generici, fino all'analisi di regressioni e failure mode e al lavoro con il team di engineering per servire i modelli in ambienti vincolati.

﻿﻿﻿

Le skill che fanno la differenza

  • Esperienza pratica vera nel fine tuning di LLM: in produzione, in ricerca applicata o in contesti sperimentali seri, con più tecniche di post-training alle spalle, idealmente SFT, LoRA e QLoRA.
  • Orientamento forte alla cybersecurity: capisci (o hai una gran voglia di capire a fondo) threat model, bug hunting e la logica di chi attacca. È il dominio su cui i modelli lavorano, e qui fa la differenza tra un buon fine tuning e uno inutile.
  • Dati prima di tutto: sai costruire, curare e mantenere dataset per training e valutazione, e sai generare, filtrare e validare dati sintetici per migliorare il comportamento del modello, non per gonfiare le metriche.
  • Stack solido: Python forte, PyTorch, Hugging Face Transformers, tokenizzazione, preprocessing e training pipeline sono pane quotidiano.
  • Dimestichezza con i vincoli reali: limiti di GPU, trade-off memoria/performance, workflow quantization-aware e ottimizzazione del training.
  • Mentalità da debugging: sai capire perché un modello è migliorato, è regredito, ha fatto overfit o ha fallito, e la valutazione la imposti su quello che conta davvero a livello operativo, non sui punteggi generici.
  • Autonomia a cavallo tra ricerca, dati ed engineering: ti muovi da solo su tutti e tre i fronti.
  • Sono Very Nice to Have: un background in software security o vulnerability research, esperienza in CTF, deploy in ambienti air-gapped, on-premise o ristretti, inference optimization, quantization, model serving o runtime LLM locali, training distribuito o multi-GPU, eval harness, red-teaming o model safety testing.

Ti manca qualcosa rispetto a quello che hai letto? Candidati comunque: siamo a caccia di game-changer, non di checklist da spuntare!﻿

Work arrangements

Il ruolo ha come sede preferenziale l'hub di Blox Space a Torino, un ambiente cost-effective e ad alta densità di persone tecniche di valore, ma valutiamo candidature da tutta Italia, con modalità operative flessibili da concordare insieme al team.
﻿Per il ruolo è previsto un range retributivo di 40.000 – 60.000 € lordi annui, con la disponibilità a valutare anche proposte superiori per profili particolarmente senior o di valore eccezionale.
﻿Sono inoltre previsti un contributo di 1.000 € per il setup dell'home office, un piano AI premium a tua scelta e retreat aziendali in Italia.

Unisciti all'ecosistema con Blox Space!

Se vuoi rendere i modelli open-weight davvero affidabili e utili contro uno dei problemi più difficili della sicurezza, e farlo accanto a chi trova bug veri in sistemi veri, questa è l'opportunità che stavi aspettando: lavorare con una delle nostre partner companies significa entrare in un team innovativo e in forte crescita, al centro di un ecosistema dove circolano idee, competenze e progetti ad alta intensità. È un ambiente dove si costruisce, si testa, si discute e si migliora ogni giorno.

jobs.description:
Role Title: Materials Scientist (Nanoparticle Sizing & Lot Release)

Role Type: Contractor

Location: Remote

micro1 is engaging Materials Scientists (Nanoparticle Sizing & Lot Release) to contribute specialized expertise to a customer’s project focused on advanced nanomaterial evaluation. In this role, you'll apply your expertise to help train next-generation AI systems. Your work will shape how models learn, reason, and perform through high-quality, real-world input. No prior experience in AI is required — your domain knowledge is what matters. This opportunity centers on thorough nanoparticle sizing, particle size distribution analysis, and lot release qualifications using Transmission Electron Microscopy (TEM) and Scanning Electron Microscopy (SEM). The engagement emphasizes independent expert analysis — including manual image thresholding, calibration, and morphology assessments — without reliance on automated or AI-powered tools. Strong written and verbal communication skills are essential to document findings, interpret complex micrographs, and convey critical decisions to project stakeholders.

Scope of Work

  1. Manually analyze and interpret TEM and SEM micrographs for nanoparticle sizing and morphological assessment
  2. Determine and document particle size distributions (PSD) with rigorous attention to accuracy and reproducibility
  3. Establish and communicate lot-release acceptance criteria based on technical reference cases and quality control standards
  4. Prepare detailed reports summarizing findings, methodologies, and recommendations for material qualification
  5. Validate measurement techniques through manual calibration, thresholding, and cross-checking against reference data
  6. Participate in technical discussions, providing expert insights on nanomaterial characterization and quality control criteria
  7. Deliver clear, concise written and verbal communications to facilitate knowledge transfer across project teams

Preferred Qualifications

  1. Advanced knowledge of nanomaterial characterization, especially using TEM and SEM
  2. Demonstrated hands-on experience in nanoparticle sizing, particle size distribution analysis, and lot release evaluation
  3. Proficiency with manual image analysis, including thresholding, calibration, and interpretation of complex morphologies
  4. Strong understanding of quality control standards and reference material qualification protocols
  5. Exceptional written and verbal communication skills for reporting and collaboration
  6. Ability to evaluate and validate technical reference cases without the use of AI-based tools
  7. Background in scientific consulting, materials science, or laboratory-based analytical roles is a plus

Preferred skills and qualifications:

jobs.description:
Position:Chief Financial Officer (CFO)

About the Role

We are seeking an accomplished and commercially strategic Chief Financial Officer (CFO) to lead the financial strategy, financial performance, capital management, investment finance, treasury, reporting, and financial governance of a diversified Insurance & Investment organization.

The CFO will serve as a key member of the executive leadership team and strategic advisor to the CEO/President and Board, providing leadership across financial planning, insurance accounting, capital and solvency management, investment portfolio performance, asset-liability management, treasury, risk, regulatory reporting, and corporate development.

The successful candidate will combine deep financial expertise with strong commercial and investment acumen and will be capable of operating in a highly regulated financial-services environment.

Key Responsibilities

1. Financial Strategy & Executive Leadership

Develop and execute the organization's overall financial strategy.

Advise the CEO, President, and Board on financial performance, capital allocation, investment strategy, and enterprise value creation.

Translate corporate strategy into financial plans, budgets, forecasts, and measurable objectives.

Lead financial decision-making across insurance, investment, and corporate operations.

Establish strong financial governance and accountability across the organization.

2. Financial Planning, Budgeting & Performance

Lead annual budgeting, forecasting, and long-term financial planning.

Develop financial models and scenario analyses to support strategic decisions.

Monitor revenue, profitability, expenses, capital efficiency, and operating performance.

Establish financial KPIs and executive dashboards.

Identify opportunities to improve profitability, efficiency, and shareholder returns.

3. Insurance Finance & Performance

Oversee financial management of insurance operations, including premiums, claims, reserves, expenses, and underwriting performance.

Monitor key insurance financial metrics including loss ratios, combined ratios, expense ratios, and underwriting profitability.

Partner with actuarial, underwriting, claims, and risk teams to assess financial performance and emerging exposures.

Ensure appropriate financial treatment and reporting of insurance liabilities and reserves.

Support pricing, product profitability, reinsurance, and portfolio decisions from a financial perspective.

4. Investment Finance & Portfolio Management

Provide financial oversight of the organization's investment portfolio and investment activities.

Partner with the CIO/Chief Investment Officer and Investment Committee on portfolio strategy and performance.

Monitor investment income, realized/unrealized gains, asset allocation, liquidity, and risk-adjusted returns.

Evaluate investment opportunities and strategic asset-allocation decisions.

Ensure investment activities are aligned with the organization's liabilities, liquidity requirements, risk appetite, and regulatory requirements.

5. Capital, Solvency & Balance Sheet Management

Lead capital planning and balance-sheet optimization.

Monitor solvency, capital adequacy, liquidity, leverage, and financial resilience.

Develop strategies to optimize the organization's capital structure and return on capital.

Assess the financial impact of major business, investment, and insurance decisions on capital requirements.

Work closely with Risk and Actuarial functions on capital and solvency assessments.

6. Asset-Liability Management (ALM)

Provide executive financial oversight of asset-liability management.

Ensure investment portfolios are appropriately aligned with insurance liabilities and liquidity requirements.

Monitor duration, interest-rate sensitivity, liquidity gaps, and market exposures.

Support development of ALM strategies and balance-sheet optimization initiatives.

Ensure appropriate financial stress testing and scenario analysis.

7. Treasury & Liquidity

Oversee treasury, cash management, liquidity planning, and banking relationships.

Maintain adequate liquidity to meet claims, operating obligations, investment commitments, and strategic requirements.

Optimize cash deployment and short-term investment strategies.

Monitor interest-rate, foreign-exchange, credit, and liquidity exposures.

Establish robust treasury policies and controls.

8. Regulatory & Financial Reporting

Ensure accurate, timely, and transparent financial reporting to the Board, shareholders, regulators, and other stakeholders.

Oversee statutory accounts, management reporting, regulatory returns, and consolidated financial statements.

Ensure compliance with applicable accounting standards and insurance regulations.

Lead relationships with external auditors, regulators, actuarial advisers, tax advisers, and other professional stakeholders.

Maintain strong financial controls and governance frameworks.

9. Risk Management & Financial Controls

Establish effective financial risk-management frameworks.

Monitor exposure to market, credit, liquidity, underwriting, operational, interest-rate, and foreign-exchange risks.

Strengthen internal controls, financial policies, and governance processes.

Work closely with the CRO, Chief Actuary, CIO, and other executives to manage enterprise-wide financial risks.

Ensure appropriate stress testing and contingency planning.

10. Reinsurance & Capital Optimization

Provide financial oversight of reinsurance strategy and economics.

Evaluate the financial and capital implications of reinsurance arrangements.

Monitor reinsurance recoverables, counterparty exposure, and profitability.

Support optimization of risk transfer, capital efficiency, and balance-sheet resilience.

11. Corporate Development & Strategic Investments

Lead financial evaluation of acquisitions, strategic investments, joint ventures, and business expansion opportunities.

Oversee financial due diligence, valuation, transaction modeling, and investment cases.

Assess potential M&A opportunities and their impact on capital, solvency, earnings, and shareholder value.

Support negotiations with investors, financial institutions, and strategic partners.

12. Investor & Stakeholder Relations

Develop strong relationships with shareholders, institutional investors, banks, rating agencies, regulators, and other financial stakeholders.

Communicate financial performance, capital strategy, investment results, and business outlook to key stakeholders.

Support investor presentations, Board materials, and strategic financial communications.

13. Finance Transformation & Technology

Modernize finance systems, reporting infrastructure, ERP platforms, and financial analytics.

Improve automation, data quality, forecasting, and management reporting.

Establish real-time visibility into financial, insurance, investment, and risk performance.

Drive continuous improvement within the finance function.

14. Leadership & Talent Development

Lead Finance, FP&A, Treasury, Accounting, Financial Reporting, Tax, and related functions.

Build a high-performing and commercially focused finance organization.

Develop finance leadership talent and succession plans.

Promote a culture of integrity, accountability, financial discipline, and business partnership.

Key Performance Indicators

The CFO will be accountable for:

Revenue and earnings growth

Operating and net profitability

Return on equity (ROE)

Return on capital

Capital adequacy and solvency

Investment portfolio performance

Investment income and risk-adjusted returns

Combined ratio / underwriting profitability

Expense efficiency

Liquidity and cash-flow management

Balance-sheet optimization

Budget and forecast accuracy

Regulatory and financial reporting quality

Cost of capital

Financial risk management

Shareholder value creation

Candidate Profile

Essential Experience

15+ years of progressive finance experience, including significant executive leadership.

Previous experience as CFO, Group CFO, Finance Director, VP Finance, Deputy CFO, or equivalent.

Significant experience within insurance, asset management, investment management, banking, pensions, financial services, or a related regulated financial institution.

Strong understanding of insurance financial statements, investment portfolios, capital management, and regulatory requirements.

Proven experience managing complex balance sheets, liquidity, capital, and financial performance.

Strong experience working with Boards, regulators, auditors, investors, rating agencies, and senior executives.

Demonstrated experience in financial strategy, investment analysis, and capital allocation.

Preferred Experience

Experience as Group CFO within a diversified insurance or financial-services group.

Experience across both insurance and investment/asset-management businesses.

Experience with life insurance, general insurance, health insurance, pensions, or reinsurance.

Exposure to institutional investment portfolios and alternative investments.

Experience with M&A, strategic investments, capital raising, restructuring, or corporate transformation.

Experience operating across multiple jurisdictions or regulated markets.

Experience interacting with insurance regulators and rating agencies.

Education & Professional Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance, Economics, Business Administration, or a related discipline.

Professional qualification such as CA, ACCA, CPA, CMA, CFA, or equivalent strongly preferred.

MBA or Master's degree in Finance/Business is an advantage.

Relevant insurance, actuarial, investment, or risk-management qualifications are advantageous.

Treasury & Liquidity

Financial Planning & Analysis

Investment Analysis

Risk Management

Insurance Accounting

M&A & Corporate Development

Capital Allocation

Investor Relations

Corporate Governance

Financial Transformation

Strategic, commercially minded, and financially rigorous

Highly analytical and investment-oriented

Experienced in highly regulated environments

Strong in capital and balance-sheet management

Comfortable engaging with Boards, regulators, investors, and rating agencies

Able to balance growth, profitability, liquidity, capital, and risk

An effective strategic partner to the CEO, CIO, CRO, and Chief Actuary

A transformational finance leader capable of building high-performing teams

The Environmental Project Manager is responsible for managing environmental projects from planning and permitting through execution and completion. This role combines project management expertise with a strong working knowledge of environmental regulations, permitting processes, and regulatory agency coordination at the federal, state, and local levels. The successful candidate will have experience managing projects involving wetland delineations and permitting, threatened and endangered species, and cultural and historic resources. They will understand how these resource areas intersect with environmental review, regulatory consultations, and permitting requirements, and will be able to coordinate the technical specialists, clients, subcontractors, and agencies necessary to advance projects efficiently and compliantly. The Environmental Project Manager is accountable for project scope, schedule, budget, quality assurance, risk management, forecasting, and client satisfaction. This individual will serve as a primary point of contact for clients, lead internal project teams, anticipate regulatory and project risks, and ensure deliverables meet applicable requirements and client expectations.

What You'll Do

  • Project and Client Management

    • Manage environmental projects from initiation through completion, ensuring deliverables meet established scope, schedule, budget, quality, and client expectations.
    • Coordinate internal resources, establish priorities and performance expectations, track milestones, and ensure timely completion of project deliverables.
    • Serve as a primary point of contact for clients, providing regular project updates, progress reports, recommendations, and solutions.
    • Lead recurring client and internal project meetings to communicate progress, address concerns, document decisions, and track action items.
    • Monitor project schedules, budgets, forecasts, expenses, and timesheets; identify variances and implement corrective actions as needed.
    • Identify project risks, manage scope changes, develop contingency plans, and escalate issues to senior management when appropriate.
    • Identify and document change orders, prepare supporting documentation, and coordinate negotiations with clients.
    • Review project deliverables for technical accuracy, completeness, quality, and compliance with contractual and regulatory requirements.
    • Maintain project documentation and follow Canacre’s established project management procedures and best practices.
    • Coordinate with Business Development to identify opportunities to expand services with existing and prospective clients.
    • Ensure applicable safety, training, and project-specific requirements are met.

    Environmental Permitting and Regulatory Compliance

    • Manage environmental permitting and compliance activities involving wetlands, waters of the United States, threatened and endangered species, cultural and historic resources, and other applicable environmental resource areas.
    • Coordinate wetland delineations and related field assessments, technical documentation, jurisdictional determinations, and permitting requirements.
    • Manage or coordinate applications and supporting documentation for permits under Section 404 of the Clean Water Act, including Nationwide Permits and Individual Permits issued by the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE).
    • Coordinate with applicable USACE Districts, federal and state resource agencies, and local authorities to advance permitting, resolve regulatory issues, and secure necessary approvals.
    • Coordinate threatened and endangered species assessments and consultations with the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (USFWS) and other applicable agencies.
    • Oversee coordination with archaeological and cultural resources subcontractors and specialists to support compliance with Section 106 of the National Historic Preservation Act and other applicable cultural resource requirements.
    • Manage environmental review and permitting activities under the National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA), including projects involving the Bureau of Land Management (BLM), as applicable.
    • Develop and implement technically sound permitting strategies that account for project design, environmental constraints, agency requirements, and regulatory schedules.
    • Advise clients and internal teams on applicable federal, state, and local environmental regulations, permitting pathways, consultation requirements, and permit conditions.
    • Integrate findings and requirements from wetlands, biological resources, cultural resources, and other technical studies into project planning, environmental documentation, and permitting strategies.
    • Coordinate technical specialists, subcontractors, clients, and regulatory agencies to resolve environmental issues and keep projects moving toward approval.
    • Track permit conditions, regulatory commitments, agency correspondence, and approval milestones to support compliance throughout the project lifecycle.
    • Support the development of stakeholder communications and project messaging, including communications involving landowners and local communities.

What You'll Bring

  • Bachelor’s degree in Biology, Environmental Science, Environmental Engineering, Natural Resources, or a related field. A master’s degree is an asset.
  • 10- 15 years experience in wetlands, threatened and endangered species, understands cultural resources and how they all relate to local, state and federal environmental permitting.
  • Experience managing wetland delineations
  • Experience with Section 404 of the Clean Water Act
  • Experience with Section 106 of the National Historic Preservation Act
  • Experience applying for Nationwide Permits or Individual Permits with the US Army Corps of Engineers (USACE)
  • Experience coordinating threatened and endangered species consultations with US Fish and Wildlife Service (USFWS)
  • Experience with NEPA relating to Bureau of Land Management (BLM)
  • Demonstrated experience managing environmental permitting projects and coordinating technical specialists and subcontractors.

jobs.description:
Before You Apply

The Opportunity

We're looking for an experienced DevOps Engineer who thrives on building secure, scalable and resilient cloud infrastructure.

You'll join an international engineering organisation responsible for the cloud platforms powering enterprise software used by customers worldwide.

Working primarily with Microsoft Azure and Kubernetes, you'll help ensure that critical applications remain secure, available and performant while making it easier for engineering teams to build, test and deploy software.

This is a hands-on role combining cloud engineering, site reliability, security and automation.

If you enjoy solving complex infrastructure challenges, eliminating repetitive tasks and improving how software is delivered, this could be an excellent opportunity.

What You'll Be Working On

Cloud Infrastructure & Kubernetes

  • Manage, maintain and optimise cloud infrastructure hosted on Microsoft Azure.
  • Operate and secure production Kubernetes environments, particularly Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS).
  • Work across cloud networking, identity management, storage and Azure SQL.
  • Maintain reliable, scalable environments supporting enterprise SaaS applications.
  • Deliver platform upgrades, patches and hotfixes while minimising disruption to customers.

Site Reliability & Performance

Reliability isn't just about responding when something breaks. It's about engineering systems that are less likely to fail.

You'll be responsible for:

  • Defining and monitoring Service Level Objectives (SLOs).
  • Implementing monitoring, alerting and observability solutions.
  • Investigating production incidents and identifying root causes.
  • Participating in on-call support and coordinating incident resolution.
  • Conducting post-incident reviews and implementing lasting improvements.
  • Testing backup, restoration and disaster recovery procedures.
  • Turning recurring operational issues into automated solutions.

CI/CD & Automation

  • Design, build and maintain automated CI/CD pipelines using Azure DevOps.
  • Integrate automated testing, quality checks and security controls into deployment workflows.
  • Improve software release processes to make deployments faster, safer and more predictable.
  • Establish standards for source control, development environments and release readiness.
  • Develop automation scripts using PowerShell, Python or Bash.
  • Reduce manual operational tasks through automation and infrastructure improvements.

Cloud Security

Security is an integral part of this role.

You'll help protect cloud infrastructure and customer environments by:

  • Identifying, prioritising and remediating vulnerabilities.
  • Managing security patches, certificates, secrets and access permissions.
  • Applying security best practices across Azure and Kubernetes.
  • Supporting secure configuration and maintenance of production environments.
  • Contributing to continuous improvements in infrastructure security.

Collaboration & Continuous Improvement

  • Work closely with software engineers and technical teams across Europe, North America and Australia.
  • Help establish and improve engineering and operational standards.
  • Share knowledge and support other engineers in adopting DevOps best practices.
  • Create and maintain operational documentation, troubleshooting guides and runbooks.
  • Contribute to a culture of reliability, automation and continuous improvement.

What We're Looking For

Essential Experience

  • 5+ years of professional experience in DevOps, Site Reliability Engineering (SRE) or cloud operations.
  • Strong hands-on experience with Microsoft Azure, including networking, identity, storage and Azure SQL.
  • Proven experience deploying, managing and securing Kubernetes in production, ideally using AKS.
  • Experience designing and maintaining CI/CD pipelines, preferably with Azure DevOps YAML.
  • Strong scripting and automation skills using PowerShell, Python or Bash.
  • Practical experience implementing monitoring, alerting and incident response processes.
  • Understanding of Service Level Objectives (SLOs) and reliability engineering principles.
  • Experience with vulnerability management, security patching and secrets management.
  • Experience supporting customer-facing production environments.
  • Familiarity with Windows Server and SQL Server.
  • Strong written and verbal English communication skills.
  • Ability to collaborate effectively with international teams across multiple time zones.

Nice to Have

Experience with any of the following would be an advantage:

Observability & Monitoring

  • Prometheus
  • Grafana
  • Loki
  • Tempo
  • OpenTelemetry

Security & Compliance

  • Microsoft Defender for Cloud
  • Azure Policy
  • ISO 27001
  • SOC 2

Deployment & Operations

  • GitOps and ArgoCD
  • Feature flag management
  • ITIL or other IT service management practices

Professional Certifications

  • Microsoft Azure: AZ-104, AZ-400 or AZ-500
  • Kubernetes: CKA or CKS

How You Work

We're looking for someone who combines strong technical expertise with a proactive engineering mindset.

You:

  • Think about reliability first. You design systems to prevent problems rather than simply reacting to them.
  • Automate whenever possible. You recognise repetitive tasks as opportunities for improvement.
  • Take ownership. You investigate problems thoroughly and follow them through to resolution.
  • Care about security. You understand that protecting infrastructure and customer data is everyone's responsibility.
  • Communicate clearly. You can explain complex technical issues to engineers and other stakeholders.
  • Keep learning. You stay informed about emerging cloud technologies, tools and engineering practices.
  • Work collaboratively. You enjoy sharing knowledge and helping your team succeed.

Why This Opportunity Stands Out

Work on infrastructure that matters

Support cloud platforms powering enterprise applications used by customers around the world.

Solve meaningful engineering challenges

Work across reliability, security, automation and cloud infrastructure rather than focusing on a single narrow area.

Make a measurable impact

Your improvements will directly influence system availability, deployment efficiency, security and the developer experience.

Collaborate internationally

Work alongside experienced engineering professionals across multiple continents.

Build for the long term

Help create reliable, secure and maintainable infrastructure that supports the continued evolution of enterprise SaaS products.

Ready for Your Next Challenge?

If you're an experienced DevOps Engineer who enjoys working with Azure, Kubernetes and modern automation technologies, we'd like to hear from you.

Apply now and help engineer the infrastructure behind tomorrow's enterprise software.

jobs.description:
Position Highlights

Overview

The CDC Foundation is seeking a candidate for a full-time Senior Health Communications Specialist who will provide strategic support, technical assistance, and communications leadership for a team working to build an evidence base for effective drowning prevention strategies in the United States. This position is key to leading the development and implementation of a strategic communication plan in support of programmatic priorities and goals. This position will also lead the implementation of a wide array of health communication and dissemination activities designed to impact positive health outcomes related to water safety and drowning prevention.

The Senior Health Communications Specialist's primary responsibility will be leading communication and information dissemination for the Understanding and Preventing Drowning program. Specifically, this position will provide support in the areas of communication planning and strategy, message development, storytelling related to program initiatives, program website development and maintenance, coordination on communication strategy and output with partner organizations, and other related activities. As the Senior Health Communications Specialist, this role will lead communications strategy and initiatives for the Understanding and Preventing Drowning team, advising senior program leadership, providing communications guidance and mentorship to other program team members, and executing the program's communications activities.

A key aspect of the Senior Health Communication Specialist role will be aligning and delivering communications and other external facing outputs across a broad program portfolio that includes several partner organizations including groups delivering swim skills training to children and youth, state and local health departments, university-based research groups, and drowning prevention and water safety organizations operating at the local, state, national, and global levels.

Duties and Responsibilities

  • Lead the development and execution of a comprehensive strategic communications plan to advance program goals. Ensure that the program's communication activities are achieved in collaboration with key partner organizations.
  • Develop and implement communications strategies that elevate program visibility, amplify key messages, and enhance engagement across earned and social media channels.
  • Lead the creation and dissemination of communications products and supporting materials for the program.
  • Support the development of a program website including working with senior program leadership, other program team members, and web developers.
  • Work with team members and external parter organizations to identify, draft, publish, and promote new stories and other information that amplify program outputs and communicate program impacts.
  • Provide communications guidance, mentorship and support to other team members, and in some cases partner organizations.
  • Advise senior program leadership and program team members on communication strategies, message framing, media engagement and other media topics as needed.
  • Ensure that documents and other content conform to organizational policies, branding and style; and align with accepted water safety and drowning prevention terminology and best-practice safety advice.
  • Coordinate with others on health media production, publications for professional and public audiences, and electronic health communication activities.
  • Manage clearance processes for communication research, evaluation, and publications.
  • Maintain robust familiarity with scientific and non-scientific literature for project-related publications.
  • Build and maintain working relationships with communications peers internal to the CDC Foundation and with external partner organizations, including donors, government health agencies and other drowning prevention and water safety organizations to enhance collaboration, align communication strategies and increase the reach of media efforts.
  • Represents the CDC Foundation at technical and strategic planning meetings with internal and external partners.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

Qualifications and Necessary Skills

  • Bachelor's degree in journalism, communications, English, public health, public policy or related field required. Master's degree preferred.
  • Minimum of 7 years of experience in the field of communications, preferably within the public health or drowning prevention-related arena, including experience developing and executing a broad range of communication and media strategies.
  • Experience independently representing organizations to media members, or past experience as a news reporter, producer, or editor.
  • Demonstrated ability to independently lead the production of communication products, documents and presentation materials that are high quality and error-free.
  • Experience working with diverse stakeholders, including senior leadership, subject matter experts, external partners and donor organizations.
  • Proven ability to collaborate with a team while also completing specific tasks independently, on task and timeline.
  • Excellent written and oral communication skills.
  • Strong understanding of communication theory and its application to strategy.
  • Experience engaging community partners and providing capacity building/skill-based support.
  • Experience working on diverse health communications and social marketing campaigns.
  • Cross-cultural competence and ability to work with a variety of partners from varying backgrounds.
  • Experience translating scientific information into easy-to-understand language for non-scientific audiences.
  • Ability to engage with, listen to and learn from a broad range of partners, encouraging meaningful participation and developing productive working relationships with colleagues and partners.
  • Strong project management skills and ability to meet deadlines, prioritize and stay organized.
  • Experience working in a virtual environment with remote partners and teams.
  • Willingness to travel domestically (up to 10% annually).
  • Experience developing and managing effective social media content that translates complex public health information into clear, engaging, and audience-appropriate messages.
  • Experience managing website content, structure, and enhancement projects, including collaborating with web developers, designers, and subject matter experts to optimize user experience.

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment and will not be discriminated against on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, mental or physical disabilities, veteran status, and all other characteristics protected by law. We comply with all applicable laws including E.O. 11246 and the Vietnam Era Readjustment Assistance Act of 1974 governing employment practices and do not discriminate on the basis of any unlawful criteria in accordance with 41 C.F.R. §§ 60-300.5(a)(12) and 60-741.5(a)(7). As a federal government contractor, we take affirmative action on behalf of protected veterans.

The CDC Foundation is a smoke-free environment.

Relocation expenses are not included.

About the CDC Foundation

The CDC Foundation is an independent nonprofit authorized by Congress to mobilize philanthropic partners to support the public health system, including the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), in preventing and responding to threats to health. In this role, we are focused on one priority: building catalytic, flexible and impactful partnerships—with corporations, philanthropies, individuals and organizations—to help improve the health and lives of people in all communities, everywhere.   • Gestión y Prospección Internacional: Identificar, abordar y cualificar prospectos e hitos comerciales en mercados internacionales para ampliar la cartera de clientes.
  • Gestión del Ciclo Integral de Ventas: Dominar de extremo a extremo el proceso comercial, desde la prospección inicial y calificación, hasta la presentación de propuestas, negociación técnica/comercial y cierre de acuerdos.

  • Coordinación de Demos y Sesiones Técnicas: Organizar y liderar reuniones técnicas con el equipo especialista para realizar demostraciones efectivas de las capacidades operativas y de soporte AMS.
  • Desarrollo de Relaciones de Confianza: Establecer, cultivar y mantener lazos de largo plazo con clientes clave, posicionándose como un asesor estratégico de negocio.
  • Cumplimiento de Metas Comerciales: Alcanzar y superar consistentemente las cuotas de ventas e indicadores clave de rendimiento (KPIs) asignados.
  • Account Management y Calidad de Servicio: Dar seguimiento continuo al estado de las cuentas activas, asegurando un nivel de servicio óptimo e identificando oportunidades de venta cruzada (up-selling y cross-selling).

Requisitos y Experiencia

  • Educación: Licenciatura o Ingeniería concluida en Administración de Empresas, Ingeniería en Sistemas, Industrial, Tecnologías de Información o carreras afines.
  • Experiencia Comprobable:
    • Mínimo 5 años de experiencia en el sector B2B de tecnología, enfocado en la comercialización de servicios de tecnología y soporte gestionado SAP (AMS).
    • Demostrada trayectoria en prospección y cierre de negocios a nivel internacional.
  • Conocimientos Deseables (Valor añadido):
    • Experiencia previa de trabajo o consultoría en ecosistemas SAP.
    • Familiaridad con metodologías Ágiles (Scrum, Kanban, Agile frameworks).

Competencias Blandas y Cualidades

  • Orientación a Resultados y Métricas: Alta motivación intrínseca por alcanzar objetivos cuantitativos y cumplir/superar las cuotas comerciales fijadas.
  • Resolución de Problemas Complejos: Capacidad analítica y criterio para destrabar situaciones comerciales y operativas de alta complejidad.
  • Curiosidad Técnica y Aprendizaje Continuo: Disposición activa y autónoma para adquirir un dominio profundo de las herramientas, arquitecturas y soluciones del portafolio.
  • Autonomía y Toma de Decisiones: Capacidad para autogestionarse, priorizar la agenda comercial y tomar decisiones acertadas en entornos remotos y dinámicos.
  • Comunicación Estratégica y Capacidad de Síntesis: Dominio de la comunicación verbal y escrita para estructurar mensajes claros, sintéticos e impactantes ante audiencias técnicas y directivas.
  • Resiliencia y Trabajo Bajo Presión: Habilidad para gestionar la frustración, adaptarse a cambios de entorno y mantener la productividad en escenarios de alta exigencia.
  • Enfoque al Cliente y Trabajo en Equipo: Alta vocación de servicio para entender las necesidades del cliente y colaborar armónicamente con las áreas técnicas internas.

About the Role

We are seeking an accomplished and commercially driven Chief Executive Officer (CEO) to lead the strategic growth, operational performance, and long-term value creation of a diversified Construction & Real Estate business.

The CEO will have overall responsibility for the organization's strategy, P&L, business development, construction operations, real estate development, investment decisions, people leadership, and stakeholder management.

The ideal candidate will be a proven senior executive with substantial experience in construction, property development, real estate investment, infrastructure, engineering, or related sectors, with a strong track record of scaling businesses, managing large project portfolios, and delivering sustainable profitability.

Key Responsibilities

1. Strategy & Corporate Leadership

Develop and execute the company's short-, medium-, and long-term corporate strategy.

Lead business expansion across construction, property development, real estate investment, and related businesses.

Identify new markets, development opportunities, strategic partnerships, and investment opportunities.

Establish clear organizational objectives, KPIs, budgets, and performance targets.

Provide strategic recommendations and regular business updates to the Board.

2. P&L & Financial Management

Take full ownership of the company's P&L, cash flow, profitability, and financial performance.

Develop annual budgets, forecasts, capital plans, and investment strategies.

Improve margins, operational efficiency, working capital, and return on invested capital.

Oversee project economics, development feasibility, financing structures, and capital allocation.

Maintain strong relationships with banks, investors, institutional partners, and other financial stakeholders.

3. Construction & Project Delivery

Provide executive oversight of the company's construction portfolio and major development projects.

Ensure projects are delivered on time, within budget, to specification, and in compliance with applicable standards.

Establish strong project governance, cost controls, procurement processes, and risk-management frameworks.

Monitor contractor, consultant, supplier, and project-partner performance.

Ensure robust health, safety, quality, environmental, and regulatory standards across operations.

4. Real Estate Development & Investment

Lead the identification, evaluation, acquisition, development, and commercialization of real estate opportunities.

Oversee land acquisition, feasibility studies, master planning, development approvals, construction, sales/leasing, and asset disposition.

Evaluate development pipelines and investment proposals based on market demand, risk, and expected returns.

Build and maintain relationships with landowners, developers, investors, government authorities, brokers, and strategic partners.

Drive portfolio optimization and maximize the value of the company's real estate assets.

5. Business Development & Commercial Growth

Develop and execute strategies to increase revenue, market share, and profitability.

Build relationships with major corporate clients, government entities, institutional investors, developers, and strategic partners.

Lead negotiations for major contracts, joint ventures, development agreements, and strategic partnerships.

Identify opportunities for diversification and new revenue streams.

Strengthen the company's market reputation and competitive positioning.

6. Governance, Risk & Compliance

Ensure the organization operates in accordance with applicable laws, regulations, contractual obligations, and corporate governance standards.

Establish enterprise-wide risk-management practices covering financial, operational, legal, construction, market, and investment risks.

Maintain strong governance across subsidiaries, projects, joint ventures, and investments.

About the assignment

We are looking for an Analytics Engineer. You'll own fraud forensics for our identity and verification platform, which verifies users through phone-number and OTP verification. We are seeing a surge in sophisticated fraud attacks on that flow, including SMS pumping campaigns targeting specific regions, while tuning critical anti-fraud thresholds where every rule change trades blocked attackers against legitimate users lost at signup. You'll investigate attacks, triage patterns, and turn findings into rules and monitoring our backend engineers can skip so they stay focused on core platform work. You'll own this space end to end while we hire a permanent team member, and leave behind detection the team can run without you.

Responsibilities

  • Fraud forensics: investigate active and past attacks on OTP and verification flows; quantify volume, cost and user impact; produce clear incident write-ups.

  • Attack triage: identify patterns across country, carrier, number range, device and attestation signals; separate SMS pumping, bot traffic and account abuse from legitimate spikes.

  • Threshold tuning: analyse and backtest anti-fraud rules and thresholds; quantify false positives (legitimate users blocked) against fraud prevented; recommend changes with evidence.

  • Detection and monitoring: turn recurring forensics into scheduled queries, dashboards and alerts so attacks are caught in hours, not after the provider invoice.

  • Engineering hand-off: give backend engineers precise, ready-to-implement rule proposals so they stay focused on platform delivery.

  • Knowledge transfer: document playbooks and coach our analytics engineer so capability stays in the team.

Requirements

Mandatory

  • 5+ years in analytics engineering, data science or fraud analytics, with at least 2 years hands-on in fraud or abuse detection.

  • Expert SQL on BigQuery: large event tables, window functions, partition-aware and cost-efficient queries.

  • Strong Python (pandas, notebooks) for ad-hoc forensics and pattern mining.

  • Building scheduled pipelines in Airflow and dashboards in Looker (or equivalent BI).

  • Experience tuning rule- or threshold-based fraud controls, including backtesting and false-positive analysis.

  • Works independently from day one; communicates findings crisply to engineers and leadership.

Nice-to-have

  • Experience investigating telecom or SMS fraud (SMS pumping / artificially inflated traffic, IRSF) at scale.

  • Hands-on with CPaaS provider logs and billing data (Vonage, Twilio, Sinch, Infobip).

  • Identity and verification domain: OTP funnels, rate limiting, velocity rules, device attestation (Play Integrity, App Attest).

  • Experience with fraud in emerging markets (Africa, South Asia), where carrier and pricing patterns differ.

  • Event streams from Kafka; streaming anomaly detection (Dataflow/Flink).

  • Statistical anomaly detection or lightweight ML (BigQuery ML, isolation forests).

We are committed to building a diverse and inclusive team. We believe a wide range of backgrounds, perspectives, and experiences strengthens our products and our culture. No matter where you're from, what language you speak, or how you identify, we value what makes you unique. This is an urgent contract engagement and we will move as soon as we find the right person, so please apply as soon as possible. jobs.description:
Position Description

Valiant Solutions is seeking an IHE Cybersecurity Compliance & Incident Response Specialist to provide senior cybersecurity compliance, breach response, incident management, and risk management support for institutions of higher education (IHEs) that handle sensitive federal data. You will help our government customer respond to cybersecurity incidents at institutions outside its system boundary, including incidents that may involve Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI), Federal Tax Information (FTI), and Personally Identifiable Information (PII). You will coordinate response and remediation, manage IHE cybersecurity cases through closure, and evaluate institutional cybersecurity compliance. Your guidance, grounded in NIST SP 800-61 Rev. 3, will help institutions strengthen how they protect sensitive federal information.

Named one of the Washington Business Journal’sBest Places to Work every year since 2014, Valiant is proud of our employee-centric culture and commitment to excellence. If you are interested in learning more about Valiant and this opportunity, we invite you to apply now!

Location: Remote with ad hoc travel to the Washington DC Metro area.

This position allows for 100% remote work. Remote work requires a high level of trust in our employees, and we strictly adhere to the details outlined in our Remote Work Policy below.

Required Clearance: Must be able to obtain and maintain a Public Trust clearance

Eligibility Requirements: U.S. citizenship is required to obtain the necessary clearance for this position.

Required Experience:

  • More than 10 years of experience in cybersecurity incident response, incident handling, cybersecurity compliance, security assessments, or cyber risk management.
  • Bachelor's degree in Cybersecurity, Information Technology, Computer Science, Information Assurance, Information Systems, Engineering, or a related technical discipline.
  • A senior industry professional certification such as CISSP or equivalent.
  • Demonstrated experience investigating, coordinating, documenting, and managing cybersecurity incidents through remediation and closure.
  • Experience conducting or supporting cybersecurity compliance assessments and evaluating technical, administrative, and physical safeguards.
  • Strong knowledge of incident containment, remediation, recovery, corrective action tracking, and cybersecurity risk management.
  • Experience evaluating security controls and identifying compliance gaps and remediation requirements.
  • Experience working with sensitive or regulated information such as CUI, PII, FTI, or comparable protected data.
  • Ability to analyze complex cybersecurity information and translate findings into clear, actionable recommendations.
  • Excellent technical writing, analytical, communication, and stakeholder coordination skills.
  • Ability to work effectively with government personnel, institutional stakeholders, cybersecurity teams, auditors, technical personnel, and organizational leadership.
  • Familiarity with NIST SP 800-61 Revision 3.
  • Strong knowledge of applicable cybersecurity regulatory and control frameworks.

Responsibilities:

Incident Response and Breach Management

  • Provide senior cybersecurity incident response and breach management support for IHEs that handle federal data.
  • Provide incident reporting and handling guidance that helps IHEs contain, remediate, and recover from cybersecurity incidents.
  • Coordinate remediation and incident response activities with reporting institutions.
  • Categorize, analyze, document, track, and manage IHE cybersecurity cases through closure.
  • Coordinate breach response activities across affected customer offices, customer contractors, IHEs, and affiliated organizations.
  • Analyze incident information and supporting evidence to identify cybersecurity risks, compliance concerns, affected data, and required remediation.
  • Track remediation activities and corrective actions through resolution.
  • Develop incident reports, technical findings, recommendations, case documentation, and status updates for customer stakeholders.

Cybersecurity Compliance and Assessments

  • Conduct and support cybersecurity compliance assessments for institutions and systems that handle federal data.
  • Evaluate the adequacy of administrative, technical, and physical safeguards and identify cybersecurity and compliance gaps.
  • Develop assessment plans that address methodology, data collection, sampling, reporting timelines, and risk-rating methodology.
  • Evaluate institutional information security programs and the implementation of required cybersecurity safeguards.
  • Review compliance audit information to determine whether identified requirements have been implemented or are addressed through acceptable corrective action plans.
  • Assess safeguards across areas including risk assessment, identity and access management, data classification and inventory, encryption, multi-factor authentication, change management and secure development, logging and monitoring, incident response capabilities, vendor and third-party risk management, and cybersecurity awareness and training.

Risk Management and Remediation

  • Identify cybersecurity risks and control weaknesses that affect how IHEs protect federal information.
  • Provide actionable remediation recommendations based on assessment and incident findings.
  • Support IHE corrective action planning and remediation efforts.
  • Provide cybersecurity consulting, threat advisories, and remediation support to participating institutions.
  • Work with institutional security teams and customer stakeholders to resolve cybersecurity and compliance issues.
  • Ensure assessment and incident response work products meet applicable agency data handling and CUI protection requirements.

Stakeholder Coordination and Technical Guidance

  • Serve as a senior cybersecurity resource to the customer and participating institutions on compliance and incident response matters.
  • Communicate complex cybersecurity incidents, vulnerabilities, compliance gaps, and remediation requirements clearly to technical and non-technical stakeholders.
  • Coordinate activities across IHE stakeholders, customer offices, contractors, cybersecurity personnel, and other affected organizations.
  • Support cybersecurity awareness activities and tabletop exercises with IHEs.
  • Provide senior guidance to less-experienced cybersecurity professionals, as assigned.

About Valiant Solutions

Valiant Solutions delivers cybersecurity and IT services to federal civilian, defense, and national security customers nationwide. We support the full cyber lifecycle, from secure system design and accreditation through AI-enabled operations, threat emulation, and continuous improvement, across classified and unclassified environments. Our work is independently certified for quality and security, including CMMI, CMMC, and ISO certifications.

Valiant is a multi-year Washington Business Journal Best Places to Work winner, and our growth and cyber leadership have been recognized by Washington Technology, Northern Virginia Technology Council, and the Triangle Business Journal. We offer strong benefits, rewards for earning industry certifications, and room to grow your career as we grow. Headquartered in McLean, Virginia, our distributed workforce supports customers from coast to coast. We go where the stakes are highest, and the margin for error is zero. If you want meaningful work alongside talented professionals, apply today.

Benefits Snapshot

Valiant takes care of the people who support our customers, with real choices in coverage and real investment in your career. Eligible full-time employees receive:

  • A choice of medical plans, from an affordable HSA option to a full-featured PPO, with generous company contributions
  • Dental and vision coverage for you and your family
  • Company-paid life, short-term disability, and long-term disability insurance
  • Optional supplemental life, accident, and critical illness coverage to round out your protection
  • 401(k) retirement plan with company match
  • Paid time off that grows with your years of service, plus paid federal holidays
  • Paid certifications, professional development, and the Valiant University training portal
  • Flexible spending accounts and a wellness and fitness program
  • Referral bonuses when you help us bring great people to Valiant

Benefit eligibility and plan details are subject to the terms of each plan and may change from time to time.

The anticipated salary range for this position is $135,000 to $150,000. This range reflects Valiant Solutions' good-faith estimate of the base salary reasonably expected for this position upon hire, at the time of posting. The range has been established based on the scope of the role, market rates, and internal equity. Where a candidate falls within the posted range will depend on job-related factors, including relevant skills, experience, qualifications, achievements, education, geographic location, applicable security clearance requirements, additional corporate responsibilities, and other legitimate, non-discriminatory business considerations. The posted range does not guarantee an offer at any particular salary. In addition to base salary, this position includes the benefits described above.

Remote Work Policy (Remote and Hybrid Positions Only)

Remote work necessitates a high level of trust in our employees. To ensure that employee performance does not suffer in a remote work environment, all employees who telecommute are expected to have a quiet and distraction-free workspace with adequate internet, dedicate their full attention and availability to their job duties during working hours, and maintain a schedule during core business hours that aligns with those of their coworkers and Valiant's clients. In alignment with Valiant's inclusive and engaging environment, cameras are encouraged and can be required to be on during virtual video conferences. Additionally, in alignment with the Office of the Inspector General’s effort to eliminate conflicting employment, all Valiant employees are required to disclose any current or future outside employment engagements. During onboarding and throughout employment, employees must disclose any current activities or intent to engage in outside employment or other professional activities and obtain written approval. Employees may not solicit or conduct any outside business during core business hours for Valiant Solutions and our clients.
