At Amgen, if you feel like you’re part of something bigger, it’s because you are. Our shared mission—to serve patients living with serious illnesses—drives all that we do.


Since 1980, we’ve helped pioneer the world of biotech in our fight against the world’s toughest diseases. Amgen is advancing a broad and deep pipeline and portfolio of medicines to treat heart disease, obesity and obesity-related conditions, rare diseases, inflammatory conditions and cancer. As a member of the Amgen team, you’ll help make a lasting impact on the lives of patients as we research, manufacture, and deliver innovative medicines to help people live longer, fuller happier lives.

Our award-winning culture is collaborative, innovative, and science based. If you have a passion for challenges and the opportunities that lay within them, you’ll thrive as part of the Amgen team. Join us and transform the lives of patients while transforming your career.


Position summary

The National Account Manager, Market Access Employer Engagement, is a strategic, external-facing member of US Market Access. Reporting to the Director, Employer Engagement - Obesity, this role leads engagement with a defined portfolio of jumbo employers and the organizations that shape their health-benefit decisions, including employer benefit consultants, coalitions, TPAs, PBMs, carriers, point-solution partners and, where relevant, IDNs. The Account Manager helps customers navigate evidence-based approaches to obesity and other Amgen therapeutic areas as assigned, with the goal of enabling appropriate patient access, sustainable benefit design and improved population-health outcomes.

This role combines consultative account leadership with deep market access expertise. The Account Manager develops account strategies, uncovers customer needs and market barriers, coordinates compliant Amgen resources, and translates field insight into enterprise strategy, evidence generation, tools and launch readiness. Success is measured by the quality and strategic depth of customer engagement, access progress within priority accounts, actionable insight and cross-functional impact - not by traditional sales call activity alone.


Key responsibilities

Own a strategic regional portfolio of priority jumbo employers and employer ecosystem accounts; create and execute account plans that define customer objectives, stakeholder maps, access barriers, value exchange, actions, measures and escalation needs.

Build trusted, senior-level relationships with employer benefits, total rewards, pharmacy, medical, finance and procurement leaders, as well as EBCs, consultants, coalition leaders, TPAs, PBMs, carriers and appropriate point-solution partners.

Lead consultative discussions on obesity benefit design, access and affordability, utilization-management approaches, patient journey and population-health outcomes, within approved Amgen strategy and compliant engagement models.

Identify and advance appropriate access opportunities through the employer decision ecosystem; coordinate with internal market access strategy, contracting, brand, medical, HEOR/RWE, value communications, patient support and field teams.

Translate Amgen clinical, economic and real-world evidence into customer-relevant value discussions; identify evidence gaps and bring actionable needs to HEOR/RWE and strategy partners.

Develop scalable employer-facing capabilities, including account tools, meeting-in-a-box content, market insights and solution concepts that support launch readiness and sustained engagement.

Monitor and communicate employer benefit, PBM, vendor, policy and competitive trends. Deliver concise, decision-ready insights that inform segmentation, account prioritization, contracting, evidence generation and brand strategy.

Represent Amgen at employer, consultant and coalition meetings and selected industry forums; expand the organization’s external presence and credibility in the employer market.

Maintain rigorous account documentation, CRM hygiene, performance tracking and compliance with all legal, regulatory, privacy and company requirements.

Conduct field sales support as necessary to drive pull through of coverage opportunities and resolve billing and coding issues related to Amgen products


Basic qualifications

· Doctorate degree and 2 years of sales, marketing, market access, employer benefits or payer experience; OR Master’s degree and 4 years; OR Bachelor’s degree and 6 years; OR Associate’s degree and 10 years; OR High school diploma or GED and 12 years of relevant experience.

· Three or more years of customer-facing strategic account management, market access, payer, employer-benefits, consulting, PBM, health-plan, coalition or relevant healthcare experience.

· Ability to travel domestically up to 60 percent of the time, including overnight travel, as business needs require.


Preferred qualifications

· Direct experience with self-insured jumbo employers, employer benefit consultants, employer coalitions, TPAs, PBMs, carriers or health-benefit point solutions.

·Demonstrated ability to influence access, coverage, benefit design, affordability or population-health decisions in a complex healthcare ecosystem.

· Strong knowledge of employer-sponsored benefits, pharmacy and medical benefit management, utilization management, managed care and contracting concepts.

·Experience in obesity, cardiometabolic disease, chronic-condition management, population health, value-based care or another complex therapeutic area.

· Ability to interpret and communicate clinical, HEOR/RWE, claims or utilization data in an executive-level, customer-relevant manner.

·Proven cross-functional leadership without direct authority, strong executive presentation skills and disciplined account-planning execution.

·MBA, PharmD, MPH or other advanced degree preferred.


Critical success profile

The ideal candidate is commercially rigorous and customer-centered: able to hold an informed conversation about affordability without reducing the relationship to price, elevate evidence without becoming academic, and coordinate the right Amgen resources without overpromising. They create value before a coverage decision, use insight to shape the enterprise, and bring disciplined follow-through to a complex, long-cycle employer market.


What you can expect of us

As we work to develop treatments that take care of others, we also work to care for your professional and personal growth and well-being. From our competitive benefits to our collaborative culture, we’ll support your journey every step of the way.

Track, report and follow up on project progress, issues, and risks to ensure timely high quality project delivery. Engage in subject matter as appropriate; perform gap and data analysis to address program gaps or deficiencies.

  3. Working knowledge of image licensing and usage terms.
  4. Comfort explaining why one choice or one price makes sense and another doesn’t.

How the selection process works

Responsibilities

This is a remote/virtual position. Candidate can be based anywhere within the United States.

Project teams in our Energy & Industrial Group (EIG) support industry-leading projects in power generation, plant design, environmental compliance, mid/downstream oil & gas, and multi-disciplined industrial projects. We are leading efforts to decarbonize the industry through advanced technologies including renewable energy, carbon capture, hydrogen, and energy storage. Our teams provide engineering and environmental services for new facilities, expansions, modifications, and operational changes at complex industrial sites.

  • As a member of Sargent & Lundy’s Environmental and Permitting team, you will apply your knowledge of the Clean Air Act and related federal, state, and local air regulations to develop practical permitting strategies for electric power and industrial projects. You will work with project managers, engineers, clients, and regulatory agencies to define, evaluate, and implement air permitting requirements throughout project development, design, construction, and operation.
  • The position will offer you the opportunity to expand your technical and project-management capabilities while working with multi-disciplined project teams to:
    • Interpret and implement federal, state, and local air quality requirements, including State Implementation Plans, New Source Review (NSR), Prevention of Significant Deterioration (PSD), nonattainment NSR, Title V, and applicable source-specific requirements.
    • Evaluate new projects and modifications for air permitting applicability, including emissions increases, significant emissions increases, major-source and major-modification determinations, contemporaneous netting, potential to-emit, and related permitting thresholds.
    • Work with project engineers and equipment vendors to identify emission units, control technologies, operating scenarios, monitoring requirements, and design criteria needed to support permit applications and compliance demonstrations.
    • Develop air permit strategies, permit matrices, schedules, and applications for major and minor sources, including construction permits, operating permits, permit amendments, exemptions, and agency notifications.
    • Prepare and review technical support documents, emissions calculations, emissions inventories, control-technology evaluations, BACT and LAER analyses, air dispersion modeling protocols and results, AERMOD inputs, and regulatory applicability memoranda.
  • Interface with federal, state, and local permitting agencies; respond to technical comments; participate in agency meetings; and support negotiations regarding permit conditions, compliance obligations, and review schedules.
  • You will have the opportunity to develop your air permitting career through peer learning, knowledge sharing with engineers and environmental professionals, and participation in Sargent & Lundy’s System of Processes and associated “Communities of Practice.”

Qualifications

We do not sponsor employees for work authorization in the U.S. for this position.

Essential skills and experience:

  • A BS in Environmental Engineering, Environmental Science, Chemical Engineering, or a related field; MS preferred.
  • Seven or more years of experience in air permitting, environmental compliance, or environmental consulting for electric power, manufacturing, oil and gas, chemical, utility, or other complex industrial facilities.
  • Strong working knowledge of the Clean Air Act and air quality regulations applicable to major sources, including NSR, PSD, nonattainment NSR, Title V, New Source Performance Standards, and National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants.
  • Demonstrated experience preparing, supporting, or reviewing air permit applications and technical analyses for new facilities, expansions, modifications, or operational changes, including:
    • New Source Review (NSR) applicability analyses for new construction and modifications, including emissions calculations, potential-to-emit, project emissions accounting, and major-source determinations.
    • Prevention of Significant Deterioration (PSD) permitting, including BACT analyses, air quality impact analyses, increment and NAAQS evaluations, and associated technical support documents.
    • Nonattainment NSR, minor-source permitting, synthetic minor strategies, permit amendments, and construction or operating permit conditions.
    • Title V operating permit applications, revisions, renewals, compliance certifications, deviation reporting, and permit-condition evaluations.
    • Preparation and review of emissions calculations, emissions inventories, source-specific emission factors, control efficiencies, and supporting spreadsheets.
    • Experience preparing or reviewing air dispersion modeling inputs and results, including AERMOD, meteorological data, receptors, building downwash, and modeling protocols.
    • Experience coordinating technical inputs from process, mechanical, electrical, and civil engineering disciplines and translating design information into permitting requirements.
    • Experience communicating with permitting agencies and supporting responses to agency comments, requests for information, and draft permit conditions.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to prepare clear technical memoranda and present permitting recommendations to clients and project teams.
  • Ability to interact effectively with project team members, clients, and regulatory agencies while managing multiple priorities and deadlines.
  • Ability to work on multiple projects at the same time and coordinate inputs between internal engineering teams, clients, and regulatory agencies.
  • Ability to provide technical guidance and mentoring to associate staff members.
  • Experience with Microsoft applications, including proficiency in Excel and Word; experience developing auditable emissions calculation tools is preferred.

Valued but not required skills and experience:

  • Experience with greenhouse gas permitting, PSD applicability for greenhouse gas emissions, climate-related permitting requirements, or carbon capture and storage projects.
    • Proficiency in ArcGIS or other mapping tools for evaluating facility locations, sensitive receptors, monitoring sites, and environmental constraints.
  • Experience with AERMOD, emissions modeling tools, or other air quality software; familiarity with state-specific permitting programs and electronic permitting systems is a plus.

Working closely with stakeholders, including business analysts, developers, and project managers this role is pivotal to ensure that solutions align with business objectives, technical standards, local regulatory requirements and our global solution design. Morgan needs to ensure that we comply with all relevant trade compliance requirements and this role will also focus on these areas, alongside other team members in other functional areas.

 

The ideal candidate will have relevant experience and a deep understanding of Microsoft Dynamics D365 across sales modules in a manufacturing environment. Strong interpersonal and communication skills, and proven experience in leading teams is essential.

 

The D365 Lead Functional Consultant for sales will take ownership of all aspects of the D365 Solution for the sales modules.

Why you're a great fit

  • Deep, current knowledge of Brazilian accounting standards (CPC / IFRS as adopted in Brazil) and Brazilian statutory and tax reporting obligations

  • Fluent in Portuguese and English, written and spoken — you'll work in Portuguese locally and in English with the US team every week

  • Able to work as the senior finance presence in Brazil with a US-based manager, across time zones

  • Strong attention to detail, clear written communication, and a habit of documenting how things work

  • Preferred but not required: working knowledge of US GAAP and experience preparing a local-to-US GAAP reporting package; experience with FIDCs, securitization vehicles, or fund accounting and CVM reporting; experience at a financial services, lending, or fintech company; experience with NetSuite; experience supporting a Big 4 or US external audit; prior experience standing up or scaling accounting operations for a foreign subsidiary

jobs.excerpt: As a Staff Product Manager for vMetal at vCluster Labs, you’ll help own the systems that discover, provision, configure, and manage physical hardware, turning racks of bare metal into a programmable platform for AI Cloud operators and hyperscalers to build tenant clusters on top of.
jobs.description:
As a Staff Product Manager for vMetal at vCluster Labs, you’ll help own the systems that discover, provision, configure, and manage physical hardware, turning racks of bare metal into a programmable platform for AI Cloud operators and hyperscalers to build tenant clusters on top of. You’ll work directly with the Head of Product and engineering leadership on the tradeoffs that shape where vMetal goes next.

As a Staff Product Manager, your role will include:

  • Infrastructure Direction: Align on business priorities and technical direction for vMetal across compute and networking, and translate that into specs engineering can execute against..

  • Networking: Own vMetal’s networking layer. Define how vMetal provisions and isolates tenant networks across InfiniBand and high-speed Ethernet fabrics, from tenant VPCs to rail-optimized GPU fabrics, and how it works with fabric controllers and NVIDIA’s networking tools.

  • Product Leadership Partnership: Work directly with the Head of Product and engineering leadership to shape the direction of vMetal.

  • Hands-on Validation: Run alpha and beta builds yourself, including against real bare metal hardware and network fabrics where possible. Catch integration issues before customers do.

  • Customer Intelligence: Engage directly with platform and network engineers at AI Cloud operators and hyperscalers running bare metal at scale, and turn what breaks in their environments into product behavior.

  • Market Positioning: Track the bare metal, GPU infrastructure, and data center networking ecosystem. Sharpen the narrative for technical buyers and bridge engineering, sales, and marketing so what we ship matches how we sell and support it.

This role could be a fit for you if you bring:

  • Experience: 5+ years experience in cloud infrastructure, data center networking, bare metal, or GPU/HPC platforms. We’re open to a range of backgrounds for this role, not just traditional product management, including networking and hardware vendors.

  • Networking Fluency: You understand InfiniBand, VLAN, VXLAN and EVPN, and BGP, and the NVIDIA networking stack (Spectrum and Quantum switches, UFM, Cumulus Linux, NVUE), well enough to make informed product tradeoffs.

  • Infrastructure Fluency: You understand bare metal provisioning, out-of-band server management (Redfish, IPMI), and PXE boot well enough to make informed product tradeoffs.

  • Customer-Facing Infra Experience: You’ve sat across from platform engineers, network engineers, and architects, and you’re comfortable in that conversation.

Bonus points for:

  • AI Networking Depth: Familiarity with fabrics tuned for GPU training or inference workloads, such as RoCEv2, rail-optimized topologies, or Spectrum-X.

  • Kubernetes-as-a-Service: Built a KaaS offering at a cloud provider, vendor, or large internal platform team.

  • Startup Growth: Adaptable to startup pace and change.

About vCluster Labs

We're the #1 platform for AI infrastructure, trusted by the world's fastest-growing AI cloud builders. We're a venture-backed startup that's raised over $28M from top-tier investors including Khosla Ventures (first investor in OpenAI, GitLab, Stripe, and DoorDash), and we're in a hyper-growth phase looking for motivated people to join our team. Our headquarters are in San Francisco (Salesforce Tower), but our team is distributed around the globe with a remote-first culture.

We give AI Cloud providers and AI factories a hyperscaler-like experience on their own GPU infrastructure. Our platform runs the full stack an operator needs, from bare metal provisioning and node lifecycle management up through managed Kubernetes, Slurm, Ray, and inference clusters, so they can turn raw GPUs into cluster products they can sell in days instead of spending 12+ months building it themselves. Today we power over 100,000 GPUs and 1 million CPUs across 50+ AI clouds and Fortune 500 companies, backed by a team of 40+ infrastructure engineers who build alongside our customers rather than just shipping them software.

We're the company behind vCluster, the open source technology for tenant isolation on Kubernetes, with 11,000+ GitHub stars and 40M+ tenant clusters created since 2021. Open source is part of our DNA. At KubeCon North America 2025, we launched our Infrastructure Tenancy Platform for AI, a Kubernetes-native framework built for running AI, ML, and GPU-intensive workloads anywhere, with an NVIDIA-validated reference architecture for DGX systems.

Benefits

We offer the following benefits:

  • Competitive Salary: We offer a competitive compensation package, including equity.

  • Premium Insurance: Health, dental, vision, and life Insurance, including plans for you and eligible dependents (benefits vary depending on country).

  • Flexible Working Schedule: You have a doctor’s appointment or need to head to the supermarket to get groceries at 2pm? We won’t have an issue with that. To us, results matter more than clocking in and out at the same time every day.

  • Workplace Flexibility: We’re very flexible about where you work. We know things can change in life and we’re happy to adjust the work environment for you along the way.

Culture & Values

At vCluster Labs, we value and stand for:

  1. Make it Happen: We have a relentless bias for action and the grit to push through obstacles. We do whatever it takes to figure it out, put in the work, and ruthlessly prioritize the actions that drive measurable impact for the business.

  2. Own the Outcome: We understand that our responsibility doesn't end when a task is checked off; it ends when the value is delivered. We connect our daily individual actions to the broader success of the company and our customers.

  3. Create Wow: We measure success by the experience we generate, both inside and outside the company. For our customers, this means impressive speed and intuitive experiences. For our team, this means going the extra mile to support one another and to continuously drive each other to new heights.

  4. Open Source, Open Mind: We are actively contributing to and maintaining open-source projects. Internally, we foster meritocracy — the strongest ideas win, no matter who or where they come from.

  5. Build Tomorrow’s Standards, Intentionally: We don't just ship software; we define the state-of-the-art of tomorrow. We are fearless in tearing down old approaches to build something better, but we are disciplined in how we do it because we know our users rely on our technology to run mission-critical infrastructure platforms.

Compensation Range: $170K - $210K

jobs.excerpt: About WonderlyWonderly is a closed-loop, end-to-end system that self-improves on our customers’ revenue.
jobs.description:
About Wonderly

Wonderly is a closed-loop, end-to-end system that self-improves on our customers’ revenue. We serve the home service industry ($1.3T), and can consistently double a new customer’s revenue within 90 days. We make all of our AI and software completely free - and only get paid when our customers make real money. We’re here helping real small businesses make a life, pay for their children’s college tuition, and live the American dream.

Pre-AI SaaS sold tools. AI companies claim they sell outcomes - task done, call answered, lead booked, ticket resolved - but calls or leads aren’t the outcomes that ultimately matter. Revenue is what ultimately matters, and today, none of the AI companies actually promise revenue. Wonderly changes that.

Our 70-person team (mostly in PDE) spent over a year building in stealth; our thesis is that - if you actually want to control the end result (revenue) of a business and deploy AI fast/cheaply, you can’t just build the sexy part (agents), you must also build the unsexy parts and own everything end to end: the system of record layer and the application layer. We built from scratch every software a home service business needs - replacing ServiceTitan, Squarespace, Ringcentral, Jobber, Square, Hubspot, and a dozen others applications. And we built every agent necessary - AI marketing, AI receptionist, AI voice, AI sales outreach, AI sales coaching, AI follow-ups, AI 3D design, AI finance, AI quoting, AI collections, and more - all embedded inside our own system with native data access. As a result, we can deploy dozens of production-ready Agents to our customers in under 24 hours with no FDEs, no integrations, and no data cleaning work.

We are the most outcome driven business model in the business because we’ve proven our system and AI Agents actually work in driving the end result - revenue. We are not trying to sell our customers a dream - each of our 10+ core AI Agents help improve our customers’ revenue by 5-20%.

Wonderly already has PMF and has gone from 0 → 1 (we are happy to share more over a call), with very clear moat and deep industry knowledge that took a team of 70 hardcore A-players 18 months to build (we are at least 2 years ahead of anyone else in the space). We believe Wonderly has the potential to be a $100B - $1T outcome. The market is massive: home service businesses across North America (a $1.3T market). We’ve raised over $50M from top-tier investors, have $20M a year in free cashflow from another product line (Motion), and all that money gets pumped into Wonderly.

About the Hiring Managers

Hi, we’re Chander and Harry, Wonderly’s CTO and CEO.

You’ll report directly to one of us. We’re looking for someone we can trust to own the operational details that keep Wonderly running—from getting the numbers right to working through a vendor contract or fixing a broken process.

You don’t need to have seen every problem before. You do need to ask good questions, exercise sound judgment, and follow through. As you build context and earn trust, you’ll take on more ownership across the business.

The Role

We’re hiring someone to own the financial and business operations behind Wonderly.

Accounting is roughly a third of the role. You’ll make sure vendors get paid correctly, coordinate month-end close with our external accountants, and keep tax requirements and financial systems organized. The rest spans contracts, procurement, insurance, equity administration, and the operational problems that come with a growing company.

We want someone with an accounting foundation who wants broad business ownership. You should be comfortable investigating an unfamiliar charge, working through a vendor renewal, coordinating with outside counsel, and building a process so the same issue is easier next time.

Your responsibilities will include:

  • Accounting operations: Validate invoices, collect vendor documentation, coordinate approvals, and schedule payments.

  • Month-end close: Keep close notes, provide supporting information to our accountants, investigate discrepancies, and flag unusual transactions.

  • Tax coordination: Keep filings, registrations, notices, and year-end reporting moving with our external providers.

  • Financial systems: Maintain tools such as Stripe, Subscript, Hubifi, and QuickBooks as the business changes.

  • Contracts and procurement: Coordinate agreements with business owners and counsel, negotiate vendor terms, and track commitments and renewals.

  • Corporate operations: Manage insurance renewals, routine equity administration, corporate records, registrations, and incoming notices.

  • Process improvement: Document recurring work, establish clear owners and deadlines, and work with our internal team to automate repetitive tasks.

You’ll have recurring responsibilities and unexpected problems. You’re accountable for closing the loop on both.

What Makes This Role Different

You’ll work directly with our CTO or CEO and see how decisions get made across the company.

Your accounting knowledge will give you a starting point, but your scope will extend across finance, legal, procurement, and corporate operations. You’ll work with accountants, lawyers, brokers, vendors, and internal teams—and be responsible for making sure work gets finished.

You’ll also have room to improve how the company operates. When something takes ten manual steps, we want you to question it, understand the constraints, and help build a better system.

As you become someone the company trusts with increasingly complex problems, your responsibilities can grow with you.

Backgrounds That Tend to Work

People from these backgrounds could thrive here:

  • Accounting or finance operations at a fast-growing startup.

  • Public accounting with hands-on exposure to startup clients.

  • Business operations roles with meaningful accounting responsibilities.

  • A broad operational role where you owned payments, contracts, compliance coordination, or financial systems.

What matters more than the resume:

  • You understand invoices, accruals, reconciliations, and month-end close.

  • You’re meticulous with money, records, and deadlines.

  • You investigate discrepancies and bring back answers.

  • You keep work moving when several people or outside providers are involved.

  • You know when to make a decision and when to involve a specialist.

  • You’re comfortable learning unfamiliar systems and handling ambiguous problems.

  • You want to use your accounting foundation across a broader business role.

Strong spreadsheet skills are expected. Experience with QuickBooks, Stripe, Brex, Carta, or similar tools is useful.

Expectations

  • 60–70 hour weeks

  • Take ownership of meaningful recurring responsibilities within your first few weeks.

  • Keep payments, filings, renewals, and other obligations organized and on schedule.

  • Give our external accountants and other specialists complete information and timely answers.

  • Raise problems early, with enough context to make a decision.

  • Handle confidential financial, employee, and company information carefully.

  • Use data, AI tools, and automation to make your work more reliable and less manual.

  • Be hands-on. Sometimes the job is improving a system; sometimes it’s calling a vendor and getting an issue resolved.

  • Expect your scope to evolve as the company grows.

Compensation

  • $100,000–$170,000 total compensation (base + equity), depending on experience.

  • Remote in the US or Canada, with regular in-person gatherings.

Wonderly is committed to creating a diverse and inclusive workplace where everyone is treated with respect and given equal opportunities. We do not discriminate based on gender identity, race, ancestry, disability, religion, sexual orientation, pregnancy status, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law. We welcome and encourage all qualified candidates to apply for our job openings.

jobs.description:
We are Local Infusion.

Local Infusion is the fastest growing infusion provider in the United States, with a mission to transform the specialty infusion industry, because patients deserve better. By providing both exceptional, patient-centered care and the proprietary, AI-driven technology powering it, Local Infusion accelerates access, simplifies workflows, and improves outcomes for everyone in the infusion journey — from patients and clinicians to health plans, health systems, employers, and pharma.

Clinicians can spend less time on paperwork and more time with patients, bringing comfort, connection, and community back to healthcare. With Local Infusion, every patient and every care team is fully supported, every step of the way.

The Role - Business Development Executive - Palm Beach (Vero Beach to Boca Raton), FL

We are seeking an experienced Business Development & Partnerships Manager to build relationships with referring physician offices (as well as other key stakeholders) to drive referral volume and revenue to our Local Infusion centers. The Business Development & Partnerships Manager will be a key representative of the Local Infusion brand in the market, and be a trusted partner to external and internal stakeholders.

Estimated Total Comp (Salary + Commission) is $200K - $235K+

Key Accountabilities

  • Grow revenue for assigned locations by driving referrals from specialist physician offices prescribing infusion therapy.

  • Develop, maintain and build relationships with key stakeholders in your territory including specialist physician office staff, primary care providers, Pharmaceutical reps, payer case managers, benefits consultants and employers.

  • Work closely with providers, referral partners, and Local Infusion operations team to ensure positive outcomes for patients and physicians.

  • Increase brand recognition by attending networking events, conferences, local walks and other community functions.

  • Act as a liaison between referring practices and Local Infusion operations team to ensure physician practices are educated on referral processes and patients are captured timely.

  • Establish a positive and collaborative working relationship with pharmaceutical reps and other referral sources within territory.

  • Input timely and well-organized reports via CRM reporting, management tracking and expense platforms.

  • Meet & exceed sales quota.

  • Occasional night and weekend work required.

  • MUST BE LOCATED IN w/in the Vero Beach to Boca Raton region

Qualifications and Requirements

  • Bachelor's degree in related field.

  • A history of meeting or exceeding sales goals.

  • Competitive spirit, with customer focused attitude.

  • Consistently positive attitude, with a commitment to ongoing self development.

  • Exceptional customer service, organizational and communication skills.

  • Excellent listening skills and ability to uncover pain points and identify opportunities.

  • Exceptional organizational skills and attention to detail.

  • Proficiency in using a Customer Relationship Management (CRM) system and standard office software application.

  • Experience working directly with physicians, nurses, and clinical staff members preferred.

  • Prior experience selling or supporting infused medications, specialty biologics, IV therapies, IG therapies, specialty injectables, or related therapeutic products strongly preferred.

  • Experience building relationships directly with physician offices, infusion clinics, specialty practices, nurses, care coordinators, and clinical staff.

  • Background calling on specialties such as rheumatology, gastroenterology, neurology, immunology, dermatology, cardiology, or similar referral driven specialties strongly preferred.

  • Proven ability to identify referral opportunities, uncover provider pain points, and identify opportunities that improve patient access, provider experience, and care coordination.

  • Travel requirements: Primarily day time travel within assigned territory, and occasional overnight travel.

  • Must be located in the Palm Beach - Vero Beach to Boca Raton area.

The Local Infusion Way

Local Infusion is a respectful, upbeat, and remote-first team united by our mission of shaping the way specialty infusion care is delivered. We are highly ambitious, but understand that in order to do a great job, we have to take care of ourselves; we expect that you will have time and energy devoted to your families, friends and hobbies.

As part of our team, full-time employees get:

  • Potential for performance bonuses

  • Medical, dental, and vision insurance through our employer plan

  • Short and long-term disability coverage

  • 401(k) — as an early stage startup, and we match!

  • 15 Days PTO — and we want you to take it!

  • Competitive paid parental leave and flexible return to work policy.

  • We invest in your career. Our company is growing quickly, and we'll give you the opportunity to do the same. You'll have access to a number of professional development opportunities so that you can keep up with the company's evolving needs and grow your career along the way.

We don’t discriminate—Local Infusion is an Equal Employment Opportunity (EEO) Employer. We fundamentally believe that a more diverse and inclusive team leads to a stronger company more able to achieve our vision.

What It's Like to Work at Local Infusion - as a Business Development Executive

jobs.excerpt: Contract | Remote, worldwide | $100-$200/hour depending on experience and location | 10-20 hrs/week Please note that eligibility may vary depending on your location, as some regions may not be supported by the client.
jobs.description:
Contract | Remote, worldwide | $100-$200/hour depending on experience and location | 10-20 hrs/week

Please note that eligibility may vary depending on your location, as some regions may not be supported by the client.

Check out this Loom video for more details:

We're looking for highly experienced software engineer (SR+) to help evaluate the quality of interactions with modern coding agents such as OpenAI Codex and Claude Code.

This is not a traditional engineering role. You won't be writing production code. You'll be evaluating something harder: whether the model thinks like a great engineer.

What this role actually is

You will assess how AI coding agents behave in real-world scenarios, focusing on:

• Whether the response makes sense

  • Whether the preamble and reasoning are useful
  • Whether the output reflects strong engineering judgment
  • Whether the interaction feels right to an experienced developer

This role is about engineering taste. Syntax correctness is the easy part.

What you'll be doing

  • Evaluate AI-generated coding interactions end to end
  • Judge whether outputs are useful, correct at a high level, and aligned with how a strong engineer would think
  • Assess the quality of explanations and reasoning, not just the code
  • Distinguish between levels of response quality (what makes something a 2 vs a 4)
  • Give clear, opinionated feedback in writing on what worked, what didn't, and what felt off or misleading
  • Help define what great looks like when working with tools like Cursor, Codex and Claude Code

What we mean by "taste"

We're looking for engineers who can answer questions like:

  • Does this feel like something a strong engineer would actually say?
  • Is this explanation helpful, or just technically correct?
  • Is the model guiding the user well, or just dumping output?
  • Would this interaction build or erode trust?

You should be comfortable making subjective but rigorous judgments, and explaining them clearly.

Who you are

  • Senior, Staff or Principal-level engineer (or equivalent experience)
  • Strong background in TypeScript/JavaScript or Python
  • Hands-on experience with at least one of OpenAI Codex, Claude Code or Cursor
  • Deep familiarity with modern AI-assisted dev workflows
  • Able to evaluate code without executing it or reviewing every line
  • Strong written and spoken English (B2 or above). You'll be writing detailed feedback and recording short video explanations, so this is a hard requirement
  • Comfortable giving direct, opinionated feedback
  • High bar for what good engineering looks like

Nice to have

  • Prior exposure to prompt design or evaluation workflows
  • Experience mentoring senior engineers or defining engineering standards

Engagement details

  • Rate: $100-$200/hour depending on experience and location

• Hours: 10-20 hours/week, flexible

  • Duration: ongoing. Projects run from about two weeks to a few months each, and we offer new ones to evaluators who do well
  • Start: as soon as you clear the take-home and a project has an open seat
  • Process: one take-home evaluation exercise with a recorded Loom walkthrough. No interview

jobs.description:
The company

Small businesses move fast. Opportunities often don’t wait, and cash flow pressures can appear overnight. To keep going, and growing, SMEs need finance that’s as flexible and responsive as they are.

That's why we built iwoca. Our smart technology, data science and five-star customer service ensures business owners can act with the speed, confidence and control they need, exactly when it's needed.

We’ve already cleared the way for 100,000 businesses with more than £4 billion in funding. Our passionate team is driven to help even more SMEs succeed, through access to better finance and other services that make running a business easier. Our ultimate mission is to support one million SMEs in their defining moments, creating lasting impact for the communities and economies they drive.

We’re looking for a Risk Analyst

You'll support & refine our lending strategy within Germany, including supporting new growth initiatives, designing & analysing tests, supporting the development of our scorecards and underwriting strategy, and managing our portfolio risk.

Working closely with data scientists, credit analysts and cross functional teams, you’ll solve analytical problems to help us provide small & medium size businesses in Germany with the funds they need to grow.

The team

The Lending Strategy team decides who iwoca lends to in Germany, and on what terms. Its work covers model development, lending strategy, and portfolio risk. The team works closely with Data Science (credit models), Product, tech teams, Operations Strategy, and our team of Credit Analysts. The team’s work is central to iwoca Germany’s growth and has a direct impact on both customer outcomes and business performance. The team includes data scientists, developers, and risk analysts, all working hybrid schedules in London.

The role

We're looking for a curious and motivated individual to join our Lending Strategy team as a Risk Analyst. You’ll work with analysts, data scientists, and senior stakeholders to shape iwoca Germany’s lending strategy.

Key responsibilities include:

  • Build expertise in the credit domain.

  • Develop your analytical skills through exposure to different experimental approaches and complex analysis.

  • Play a leading role in providing insightful analytics on the risk profile of our lending book and assisting with lending strategy decisions.

  • Partner with key stakeholders within Team Germany in order to provide credit risk expertise to multi-disciplinary projects.

  • Work closely with the data science teams to improve our credit assessment scorecards & strategies (both for our automated and manual underwriting processes).

  • Develop and maintain reporting dashboards, presenting a clear picture of the state of our lending.

  • Practice turning data into information, and information into insights, so that you and various stakeholders can deliver improvements with real impact for our customers.

The requirements

We look for people that are smart, humble, motivated and who are always looking to improve.

Essential:

  • A degree in a quantitative field such as Mathematics, Physics, Engineering, or similar.

  • Ability to analyse data and generate insights to support decisions.

  • Clear written and verbal communication, with the ability to tailor analysis and recommendations to different audiences.

  • An analytical mindset with a practical approach to problem solving.

  • A bucket-load of common sense.

  • A commitment to using modern tools effectively – including AI – to maximise quality, speed, and rigour, while retaining responsibility for accuracy and outcomes.

Bonus:

  • Experience in B2B or B2C credit risk lending and strategy.

  • Experience with SQL and Python

  • Experience with data visualisation tools like Looker

The salary

We expect to pay from £40,000–£55,000 for this role. But, we’re open-minded, so definitely include your salary goals with your application. We routinely benchmark salaries against market rates, and run quarterly performance and salary reviews.

The culture

At iwoca, we prioritise a culture of learning, growth, and support, and invest in the development of our team members. We value thought and skill diversity, and encourage people to explore new areas of interest, adopt better tools – including AI – and apply sound judgement so our products and decisions improve over time.

The offices

We put a lot of effort into making iwoca a great place to work:

  • Offices in London, Leeds, Berlin, and Frankfurt with plenty of drinks and snacks.

  • Events and community-led groups, including running groups, padel, and monthly ping-pong and pool competitions.

The benefits

  • Flexible working hours.

  • Medical insurance from Vitality, including discounted gym membership.

  • A choice between a dedicated dental plan or a health cash plan that reimburses everyday medical expenses.

  • A private GP service (separate from Vitality) for you, your partner, and your dependents.

  • 25 days’ holiday per year, an extra day off for your birthday, the option to buy or sell an additional five days of annual leave, and unlimited unpaid leave.

  • A one-month, fully paid sabbatical after four years.

  • Instant access to external counselling and therapy sessions for team members that need emotional or mental health support.

  • 3% Pension contributions on total earnings.

  • An employee equity incentive scheme.

  • Generous parental leave and a nursery tax benefit scheme to help you save money.

  • Electric car scheme and cycle to work scheme.

  • Two company retreats a year: we’ve been to France, Italy, Spain, and further afield.

And to make sure we all keep learning, we offer:

  • A learning and development budget for everyone.

  • Company-wide talks with internal and external speakers.

  • Access to learning platforms like Treehouse.

Director of Clinical Reimbursement, Skilled Nursing
Location: [Remote US] · Travel: As needed to key clientele (10%)

About Teton.ai

Teton is building the predictive intelligence layer for senior care. Our AI and computer vision platform passively and privately understands what is happening across residents, staff and space, then turns it into actionable insight for frontline caregivers, operators and owners.

Founded in Copenhagen in 2020 and backed by a $20M Series A led by Plural, Teton is used every month by more than 10,000 care staff across the US and Europe. Operators running Teton report 50–70% fewer falls and a 20% reduction in temporary and night staffing. We are now scaling across US skilled nursing and senior living portfolios.

The role

The Director of Clinical Reimbursement, Skilled Nursing is Teton's senior authority on the RAI process, the MDS 3.0 and PDPM. You will translate deep regional and national reimbursement expertise into Teton's product, so the care our platform observes is accurately reflected in assessments, documentation and revenue.

You will sit at the intersection of clinical operations, product and customers. Your work shapes what we build, how we prove value to SNF operators, and how our clients capture the reimbursement their care already earns, compliantly.


What you'll do

Translate RAI and MDS expertise into product

  • Serve as Teton's subject-matter expert on the RAI Manual, MDS 3.0, PDPM, Section GG, Care Area Assessments and Quality Measures.

  • Map what Teton's platform observes (mobility, ADLs, sleep, falls, behaviors, staff interactions) to MDS items, look-back periods and PDPM components.

  • Define clinical and reimbursement requirements with product, data science and engineering; write specs, review models and validate outputs against real assessments.

  • Monitor CMS rule changes, RAI Manual updates, Five-Star and SNF VBP changes, and state Medicaid case-mix methodologies, and turn them into product roadmap input.

Protect accuracy and compliance

  • Ensure every reimbursement-related insight Teton delivers is defensible, audit-ready and supported by documentation.

  • Build guardrails that prevent upcoding and flag under-capture, so clients capture accurate reimbursement, not inflated reimbursement.

jobs.excerpt: Position:Chief Financial Officer (CFO) About the RoleWe are seeking an accomplished and commercially strategic Chief Financial Officer (CFO) to lead the financial strategy, financial performance, capital management, investment finance, treasury, reporting, and financial governance of a diversified Insurance & Investment organization.
jobs.description:
Position:Chief Financial Officer (CFO)

About the Role

We are seeking an accomplished and commercially strategic Chief Financial Officer (CFO) to lead the financial strategy, financial performance, capital management, investment finance, treasury, reporting, and financial governance of a diversified Insurance & Investment organization.

The CFO will serve as a key member of the executive leadership team and strategic advisor to the CEO/President and Board, providing leadership across financial planning, insurance accounting, capital and solvency management, investment portfolio performance, asset-liability management, treasury, risk, regulatory reporting, and corporate development.

The successful candidate will combine deep financial expertise with strong commercial and investment acumen and will be capable of operating in a highly regulated financial-services environment.

Key Responsibilities

1. Financial Strategy & Executive Leadership

Develop and execute the organization's overall financial strategy.

Advise the CEO, President, and Board on financial performance, capital allocation, investment strategy, and enterprise value creation.

Translate corporate strategy into financial plans, budgets, forecasts, and measurable objectives.

Lead financial decision-making across insurance, investment, and corporate operations.

Establish strong financial governance and accountability across the organization.

2. Financial Planning, Budgeting & Performance

Lead annual budgeting, forecasting, and long-term financial planning.

Develop financial models and scenario analyses to support strategic decisions.

Monitor revenue, profitability, expenses, capital efficiency, and operating performance.

Establish financial KPIs and executive dashboards.

Identify opportunities to improve profitability, efficiency, and shareholder returns.

3. Insurance Finance & Performance

Oversee financial management of insurance operations, including premiums, claims, reserves, expenses, and underwriting performance.

Monitor key insurance financial metrics including loss ratios, combined ratios, expense ratios, and underwriting profitability.

Partner with actuarial, underwriting, claims, and risk teams to assess financial performance and emerging exposures.

Ensure appropriate financial treatment and reporting of insurance liabilities and reserves.

Support pricing, product profitability, reinsurance, and portfolio decisions from a financial perspective.

4. Investment Finance & Portfolio Management

Provide financial oversight of the organization's investment portfolio and investment activities.

Partner with the CIO/Chief Investment Officer and Investment Committee on portfolio strategy and performance.

Monitor investment income, realized/unrealized gains, asset allocation, liquidity, and risk-adjusted returns.

Evaluate investment opportunities and strategic asset-allocation decisions.

Ensure investment activities are aligned with the organization's liabilities, liquidity requirements, risk appetite, and regulatory requirements.

5. Capital, Solvency & Balance Sheet Management

Lead capital planning and balance-sheet optimization.

Monitor solvency, capital adequacy, liquidity, leverage, and financial resilience.

Develop strategies to optimize the organization's capital structure and return on capital.

Assess the financial impact of major business, investment, and insurance decisions on capital requirements.

Work closely with Risk and Actuarial functions on capital and solvency assessments.

6. Asset-Liability Management (ALM)

Provide executive financial oversight of asset-liability management.

Ensure investment portfolios are appropriately aligned with insurance liabilities and liquidity requirements.

Monitor duration, interest-rate sensitivity, liquidity gaps, and market exposures.

Support development of ALM strategies and balance-sheet optimization initiatives.

Ensure appropriate financial stress testing and scenario analysis.

7. Treasury & Liquidity

Oversee treasury, cash management, liquidity planning, and banking relationships.

Maintain adequate liquidity to meet claims, operating obligations, investment commitments, and strategic requirements.

Optimize cash deployment and short-term investment strategies.

Monitor interest-rate, foreign-exchange, credit, and liquidity exposures.

Establish robust treasury policies and controls.

8. Regulatory & Financial Reporting

Ensure accurate, timely, and transparent financial reporting to the Board, shareholders, regulators, and other stakeholders.

Oversee statutory accounts, management reporting, regulatory returns, and consolidated financial statements.

Ensure compliance with applicable accounting standards and insurance regulations.

Lead relationships with external auditors, regulators, actuarial advisers, tax advisers, and other professional stakeholders.

Maintain strong financial controls and governance frameworks.

9. Risk Management & Financial Controls

Establish effective financial risk-management frameworks.

Monitor exposure to market, credit, liquidity, underwriting, operational, interest-rate, and foreign-exchange risks.

Strengthen internal controls, financial policies, and governance processes.

Work closely with the CRO, Chief Actuary, CIO, and other executives to manage enterprise-wide financial risks.

Ensure appropriate stress testing and contingency planning.

10. Reinsurance & Capital Optimization

Provide financial oversight of reinsurance strategy and economics.

Evaluate the financial and capital implications of reinsurance arrangements.

Monitor reinsurance recoverables, counterparty exposure, and profitability.

Support optimization of risk transfer, capital efficiency, and balance-sheet resilience.

11. Corporate Development & Strategic Investments

Lead financial evaluation of acquisitions, strategic investments, joint ventures, and business expansion opportunities.

Oversee financial due diligence, valuation, transaction modeling, and investment cases.

Assess potential M&A opportunities and their impact on capital, solvency, earnings, and shareholder value.

Support negotiations with investors, financial institutions, and strategic partners.

12. Investor & Stakeholder Relations

Develop strong relationships with shareholders, institutional investors, banks, rating agencies, regulators, and other financial stakeholders.

Communicate financial performance, capital strategy, investment results, and business outlook to key stakeholders.

Support investor presentations, Board materials, and strategic financial communications.

13. Finance Transformation & Technology

Modernize finance systems, reporting infrastructure, ERP platforms, and financial analytics.

Improve automation, data quality, forecasting, and management reporting.

Establish real-time visibility into financial, insurance, investment, and risk performance.

Drive continuous improvement within the finance function.

14. Leadership & Talent Development

Lead Finance, FP&A, Treasury, Accounting, Financial Reporting, Tax, and related functions.

Build a high-performing and commercially focused finance organization.

Develop finance leadership talent and succession plans.

Promote a culture of integrity, accountability, financial discipline, and business partnership.

Key Performance Indicators

The CFO will be accountable for:

Revenue and earnings growth

Operating and net profitability

Return on equity (ROE)

Return on capital

Capital adequacy and solvency

Investment portfolio performance

Investment income and risk-adjusted returns

Combined ratio / underwriting profitability

Expense efficiency

Liquidity and cash-flow management

Balance-sheet optimization

Budget and forecast accuracy

Regulatory and financial reporting quality

Cost of capital

Financial risk management

Shareholder value creation

Candidate Profile

Essential Experience

15+ years of progressive finance experience, including significant executive leadership.

Previous experience as CFO, Group CFO, Finance Director, VP Finance, Deputy CFO, or equivalent.

Significant experience within insurance, asset management, investment management, banking, pensions, financial services, or a related regulated financial institution.

Strong understanding of insurance financial statements, investment portfolios, capital management, and regulatory requirements.

Proven experience managing complex balance sheets, liquidity, capital, and financial performance.

Strong experience working with Boards, regulators, auditors, investors, rating agencies, and senior executives.

Demonstrated experience in financial strategy, investment analysis, and capital allocation.

Preferred Experience

Experience as Group CFO within a diversified insurance or financial-services group.

Experience across both insurance and investment/asset-management businesses.

Experience with life insurance, general insurance, health insurance, pensions, or reinsurance.

Exposure to institutional investment portfolios and alternative investments.

Experience with M&A, strategic investments, capital raising, restructuring, or corporate transformation.

Experience operating across multiple jurisdictions or regulated markets.

Experience interacting with insurance regulators and rating agencies.

Education & Professional Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance, Economics, Business Administration, or a related discipline.

Professional qualification such as CA, ACCA, CPA, CMA, CFA, or equivalent strongly preferred.

MBA or Master's degree in Finance/Business is an advantage.

Relevant insurance, actuarial, investment, or risk-management qualifications are advantageous.

Core Competencies

Insurance Finance

Corporate Finance

Investment Finance

Capital & Solvency Management

Asset-Liability Management

Treasury & Liquidity

Financial Planning & Analysis

Investment Analysis

Financial Modeling

Risk Management

Regulatory Reporting

Insurance Accounting

M&A & Corporate Development

Capital Allocation

Investor Relations

Corporate Governance

Financial Transformation

Leadership Characteristics

The successful CFO will be:

Strategic, commercially minded, and financially rigorous

Highly analytical and investment-oriented

Experienced in highly regulated environments

Strong in capital and balance-sheet management

Comfortable engaging with Boards, regulators, investors, and rating agencies

Able to balance growth, profitability, liquidity, capital, and risk

An effective strategic partner to the CEO, CIO, CRO, and Chief Actuary

Strong in complex financial decision-making

A transformational finance leader capable of building high-performing teams

Compensation

A competitive executive compensation package comprising base salary, performance-based incentives, executive benefits, and other benefits commensurate with experience and market benchmarks.

jobs.excerpt: As Head of Content at vCluster Labs, you aren’t just publishing blog posts; you are building the content engine that makes vCluster Labs the reference point for how AI clouds and enterprises build and run AI infrastructure.
jobs.description:
As Head of Content at vCluster Labs, you aren’t just publishing blog posts; you are building the content engine that makes vCluster Labs the reference point for how AI clouds and enterprises build and run AI infrastructure. You’ll own content strategy across every buying stage, our SEO and AI answer engine presence, and the flagship thought leadership that defines the category. You’ll measure all of it in trials, demos and influenced pipeline. You write and edit at an expert level, and you use modern AI tools to ship deeply technical work at a quality and pace a traditional team can’t match. Strong product marketing, DevRel, creative and ecosystem teams are already in place, and your job is to put them on one calendar that drives growth.

As Head of Content, your role will include:

  • Content Strategy by Buying Stage: You will map content to the questions buyers ask at each stage. Early on, they ask why the software layer matters to an AI cloud or an enterprise AI Factory. Then they ask how the best teams deliver a hyperscaler experience on their own hardware, and finally who else runs this in production. You’ll build separate tracks for AI cloud providers and enterprise buyers, including telcos launching GPU services, Fortune 500 AI Factories and platform teams running clusters across public and private cloud. You’ll also supply each quarterly campaign kit and the Field and ABM team with business cases, account-tailored pages, event follow-ups and nurture content.

  • SEO & AEO Engine: You will lead search and AI answer engine strategy across our core topic clusters: managed clusters for AI clouds, Slurm and HPC, tenant isolation, bare metal and infrastructure, inference, and AI cloud economics. On the enterprise side, that includes return on AI infrastructure investment and one tenant experience across EKS, GKE, AKS and bare metal. Each cluster gets a pillar page, supporting technical posts and a clear path to a free trial, demo or conversation.

  • Flagship Thought Leadership: You will own the annual State of the AI Cloud report and the content chapters of our year-long brand campaign. You’ll ghostwrite and place bylines, talks and points of view for our CEO and CTO, and build our enterprise narrative for AI Factories, telcos and platform teams.

  • Content Production & Proof: You will run one content calendar with DevRel and Product Marketing. You’ll ramp to 2 to 3 SEO-led technical posts per week, one webinar per month, two benchmarks or reference architectures a year and four new customer stories a year, including a telco and an AI Factory. You’ll also build the AI-assisted workflows for research, drafting, technical review and repurposing that let a small team hit this volume without lowering the bar.

  • Quality & Measurement: You will hold the bar on every claim: grounded in approved proof, technically correct, on brand and precise about the specific isolation boundary. You’ll baseline organic, AI referral and conversion metrics, set targets, and report content’s contribution to sourced and influenced pipeline.

  • Early Impact: In your first 30 days, you’ll complete an SEO and AEO audit and deliver a prioritized plan. Within 3 months, organic and AI referral traffic will grow and convert better to trials, demos and conversations, and vCluster Labs will appear in AI answer engine results for our top category prompts. By the end of 2027, content will be attached to a growing share of Tier 1 and Tier 2 opportunities.

This role could be a fit for you if you bring:

  • Content Leadership: 10+ years in B2B content marketing, including at least 5 years leading content strategy for technical or infrastructure products sold to enterprise buyers. Your portfolio shows both category-defining thought leadership and content that measurably drove pipeline.

  • Writing & Editing Craft: You can interview a principal engineer and turn it into a piece a CTO forwards.

  • Search Expertise: Deep, current SEO experience and a working point of view on AEO and generative search. You’re fluent in GA4, Search Console, Ahrefs or Semrush, and a CMS such as Webflow.

  • AI-Native Content Production: You use AI tools such as Claude, alongside research, SEO and AEO platforms, to produce deeply technical content of exceptional quality. You know where these tools speed you up, where they fall short, and how to verify every technical claim before it ships.

  • Technical Curiosity: You’re comfortable with cloud infrastructure, Kubernetes, HPC or GPU computing concepts, and you want to go deeper.

  • Cross-Functional Leadership: Experience running a content calendar across DevRel, Product Marketing, freelancers and agencies.

Bonus points for:

  • AI & Developer Markets: Experience in AI infrastructure, open source or developer tools, including marketing to enterprise platform engineering and infrastructure teams.

  • Research & Analyst Relations: Experience producing research reports or working with industry analysts.

  • Executive Voice: A track record of executive ghostwriting and media placement.

About vCluster Labs

We're the #1 platform for AI infrastructure, trusted by the world's fastest-growing AI cloud builders. We're a venture-backed startup that's raised over $28M from top-tier investors including Khosla Ventures (first investor in OpenAI, GitLab, Stripe, and DoorDash), and we're in a hyper-growth phase looking for motivated people to join our team. Our headquarters are in San Francisco (Salesforce Tower), but our team is distributed around the globe with a remote-first culture.

We give AI Cloud providers and AI factories a hyperscaler-like experience on their own GPU infrastructure. Our platform runs the full stack an operator needs, from bare metal provisioning and node lifecycle management up through managed Kubernetes, Slurm, Ray, and inference clusters, so they can turn raw GPUs into cluster products they can sell in days instead of spending 12+ months building it themselves. Today we power over 100,000 GPUs and 1 million CPUs across 50+ AI clouds and Fortune 500 companies, backed by a team of 40+ infrastructure engineers who build alongside our customers rather than just shipping them software.

We're the company behind vCluster, the open source technology for tenant isolation on Kubernetes, with 11,000+ GitHub stars and 40M+ tenant clusters created since 2021. Open source is part of our DNA. At KubeCon North America 2025, we launched our Infrastructure Tenancy Platform for AI, a Kubernetes-native framework built for running AI, ML, and GPU-intensive workloads anywhere, with an NVIDIA-validated reference architecture for DGX systems.

Benefits

We offer the following benefits:

  • Competitive Salary: We offer a competitive compensation package, including equity.

  • Premium Insurance: Health, dental, vision, and life Insurance, including plans for you and eligible dependents (benefits vary depending on country).

  • Flexible Working Schedule: You have a doctor’s appointment or need to head to the supermarket to get groceries at 2pm? We won’t have an issue with that. To us, results matter more than clocking in and out at the same time every day.

  • Workplace Flexibility: We’re very flexible about where you work. We know things can change in life and we’re happy to adjust the work environment for you along the way.

Culture & Values

At vCluster Labs, we value and stand for:

  1. Make it Happen: We have a relentless bias for action and the grit to push through obstacles. We do whatever it takes to figure it out, put in the work, and ruthlessly prioritize the actions that drive measurable impact for the business.

  2. Own the Outcome: We understand that our responsibility doesn't end when a task is checked off; it ends when the value is delivered. We connect our daily individual actions to the broader success of the company and our customers.

  3. Create Wow: We measure success by the experience we generate, both inside and outside the company. For our customers, this means impressive speed and intuitive experiences. For our team, this means going the extra mile to support one another and to continuously drive each other to new heights.

  4. Open Source, Open Mind: We are actively contributing to and maintaining open-source projects. Internally, we foster meritocracy — the strongest ideas win, no matter who or where they come from.

  5. Build Tomorrow’s Standards, Intentionally: We don't just ship software; we define the state-of-the-art of tomorrow. We are fearless in tearing down old approaches to build something better, but we are disciplined in how we do it because we know our users rely on our technology to run mission-critical infrastructure platforms.

Compensation Range: $150K - $175K

jobs.description:
About Wonderly

Wonderly is a closed-loop, end-to-end system that self-improves on our customers’ revenue. We serve the home service industry ($1.3T), and can consistently double a new customer’s revenue within 90 days. We make all of our AI and software completely free - and only get paid when our customers make real money. We’re here helping real small businesses make a life, pay for their children’s college tuition, and live the American dream.

Pre-AI SaaS sold tools. AI companies claim they sell outcomes - task done, call answered, lead booked, ticket resolved - but calls or leads aren’t the outcomes that ultimately matter. Revenue is what ultimately matters, and today, none of the AI companies actually promise revenue. Wonderly changes that.

Our 70-person team (mostly in PDE) spent over a year building in stealth; our thesis is that - if you actually want to control the end result (revenue) of a business and deploy AI fast/cheaply, you can’t just build the sexy part (agents), you must also build the unsexy parts and own everything end to end: the system of record layer and the application layer. We built from scratch every software a home service business needs - replacing ServiceTitan, Squarespace, Ringcentral, Jobber, Square, Hubspot, and a dozen others applications. And we built every agent necessary - AI marketing, AI receptionist, AI voice, AI sales outreach, AI sales coaching, AI follow-ups, AI 3D design, AI finance, AI quoting, AI collections, and more - all embedded inside our own system with native data access. As a result, we can deploy dozens of production-ready Agents to our customers in under 24 hours with no FDEs, no integrations, and no data cleaning work.

We are the most outcome driven business model in the business because we’ve proven our system and AI Agents actually work in driving the end result - revenue. We are not trying to sell our customers a dream - each of our 10+ core AI Agents help improve our customers’ revenue by 5-20%.

Wonderly already has PMF and has gone from 0 → 1 (we are happy to share more over a call), with very clear moat and deep industry knowledge that took a team of 70 hardcore A-players 18 months to build (we are at least 2 years ahead of anyone else in the space). We believe Wonderly has the potential to be a $100B - $1T outcome. The market is massive: home service businesses across North America (a $1.3T market). We’ve raised over $50M from top-tier investors, have $20M a year in free cashflow from another product line (Motion), and all that money gets pumped into Wonderly.

About the Hiring Managers

Hi, we’re Chander and Harry, Wonderly’s CTO and CEO.

You’ll report directly to one of us. We’re looking for someone we can trust to own the operational details that keep Wonderly running—from getting the numbers right to working through a vendor contract or fixing a broken process.

You don’t need to have seen every problem before. You do need to ask good questions, exercise sound judgment, and follow through. As you build context and earn trust, you’ll take on more ownership across the business.

The Role

We’re hiring someone to own the financial and business operations behind Wonderly.

Accounting is roughly a third of the role. You’ll make sure vendors get paid correctly, coordinate month-end close with our external accountants, and keep tax requirements and financial systems organized. The rest spans contracts, procurement, insurance, equity administration, and the operational problems that come with a growing company.

We want someone with an accounting foundation who wants broad business ownership. You should be comfortable investigating an unfamiliar charge, working through a vendor renewal, coordinating with outside counsel, and building a process so the same issue is easier next time.

Your responsibilities will include:

  • Accounting operations: Validate invoices, collect vendor documentation, coordinate approvals, and schedule payments.

  • Month-end close: Keep close notes, provide supporting information to our accountants, investigate discrepancies, and flag unusual transactions.

  • Tax coordination: Keep filings, registrations, notices, and year-end reporting moving with our external providers.

  • Financial systems: Maintain tools such as Stripe, Subscript, Hubifi, and QuickBooks as the business changes.

  • Contracts and procurement: Coordinate agreements with business owners and counsel, negotiate vendor terms, and track commitments and renewals.

  • Corporate operations: Manage insurance renewals, routine equity administration, corporate records, registrations, and incoming notices.

  • Process improvement: Document recurring work, establish clear owners and deadlines, and work with our internal team to automate repetitive tasks.

You’ll have recurring responsibilities and unexpected problems. You’re accountable for closing the loop on both.

What Makes This Role Different

You’ll work directly with our CTO or CEO and see how decisions get made across the company.

Your accounting knowledge will give you a starting point, but your scope will extend across finance, legal, procurement, and corporate operations. You’ll work with accountants, lawyers, brokers, vendors, and internal teams—and be responsible for making sure work gets finished.

You’ll also have room to improve how the company operates. When something takes ten manual steps, we want you to question it, understand the constraints, and help build a better system.

As you become someone the company trusts with increasingly complex problems, your responsibilities can grow with you.

Backgrounds That Tend to Work

People from these backgrounds could thrive here:

  • Accounting or finance operations at a fast-growing startup.

  • Public accounting with hands-on exposure to startup clients.

  • Business operations roles with meaningful accounting responsibilities.

  • A broad operational role where you owned payments, contracts, compliance coordination, or financial systems.

What matters more than the resume:

  • You understand invoices, accruals, reconciliations, and month-end close.

  • You’re meticulous with money, records, and deadlines.

  • You investigate discrepancies and bring back answers.

  • You keep work moving when several people or outside providers are involved.

  • You know when to make a decision and when to involve a specialist.

  • You’re comfortable learning unfamiliar systems and handling ambiguous problems.

  • You want to use your accounting foundation across a broader business role.

Strong spreadsheet skills are expected. Experience with QuickBooks, Stripe, Brex, Carta, or similar tools is useful.

Expectations

  • 60–70 hour weeks

  • Take ownership of meaningful recurring responsibilities within your first few weeks.

  • Keep payments, filings, renewals, and other obligations organized and on schedule.

  • Give our external accountants and other specialists complete information and timely answers.

  • Raise problems early, with enough context to make a decision.

  • Handle confidential financial, employee, and company information carefully.

  • Use data, AI tools, and automation to make your work more reliable and less manual.

  • Be hands-on. Sometimes the job is improving a system; sometimes it’s calling a vendor and getting an issue resolved.

  • Expect your scope to evolve as the company grows.

Compensation

  • $100,000–$170,000 total compensation (base + equity), depending on experience.

  • Remote in the US or Canada, with regular in-person gatherings.

Wonderly is committed to creating a diverse and inclusive workplace where everyone is treated with respect and given equal opportunities. We do not discriminate based on gender identity, race, ancestry, disability, religion, sexual orientation, pregnancy status, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law. We welcome and encourage all qualified candidates to apply for our job openings.

About the Company

Our client is a Series B enterprise AI startup that raised $108M from a16z, Benchmark, First Round, BoxGroup, and YC, building infrastructure that turns complex documents into structured, AI-ready data. Its API-based platform processes PDFs, images, spreadsheets, and other unstructured files, helping organizations build production AI applications and automate document-intensive workflows.

Our client supports AI-native startups and large enterprises with demanding accuracy and deployment requirements. The team is founder-led and engineering-first, with engineers working directly with customers and using what they learn to improve the product.

The Mission

Make complex document data reliable enough to build on.

Our client helps organizations unlock information inside unstructured files while preserving the detail and structure that downstream applications depend on. The goal is to deliver accurate, usable data that holds up in production, not simply extract text that looks convincing in a demo.

Own the technical work that turns an enterprise evaluation into a successful production deployment.

As a Forward Deployed Engineer, you’ll build applications, run evaluations, troubleshoot integrations, and stay close to customer results. You’ll partner with sales during technical evaluations, then own technical success for 1-3 enterprise accounts, helping customers resolve issues, deepen adoption, and expand into additional use cases.

This is a founding role within our client’s developing FDE function. You’ll work directly with founders, product, and engineering to shape the platform and establish how future deployments are delivered.

The role combines substantial engineering work with customer relationships and deployment responsibility. Both backend-leaning engineers and customer-facing FDEs are welcome, but independent coding and production deployment ownership are essential. This position requires full-time, in-person work in San Francisco, five days per week.

What You'll Do

  • Turn customer requirements into working applications and integrations

  • Partner with AEs and SEs on evaluations, custom demos, and competitive benchmarking

  • Own technical success for 1-3 enterprise accounts, meeting weekly or biweekly
